docs.title: Portfolio Breakdown
docs.text:
Understand what you own, how it is allocated, and how a proposed contribution would change it. Portfolio Breakdown runs locally, in a standalone window or in your browser. It supports current holdings, hierarchical categories, ETF exposure and planning; it does not execute trades or calculate taxes.

Start with installation, then explore the demo or create an empty portfolio. For an existing holdings report, use the reviewed import.

What you want to do Guide Set strategic categories and targets Allocation Record quantities and remaining buy-in costs Positions Connect imported holdings to market quotes Live listings See direct and indirect holdings together Exposure and ETFs Understand prices, gains and missing values Prices and performance Interpret historical risk and fund metrics Analytics Track moving averages and account thresholds Monitoring and alerts Preview a contribution or rebalance Rebalance Review transaction history and reconstructed balances Import transactions Record futures and account financing Futures and leverage Upgrade an existing installation Release and upgrade notes Back up, restore or move your data Storage and recovery Resolve a problem Troubleshooting

docs.title: Which documentation applies?
docs.text:
Each built page identifies its source commit, application package version and channel. Development follows ongoing work. Candidate and release copies refer to fixed source commits. Use the help linked by your installed version; a newer development guide may describe different controls.

This guide covers version 0.2.0, including optional transaction history, personal performance, monitoring, and actual-account recording in EUR/USD/GBP. The release notes explain the changes and upgrade precautions. A package version alone may be shared by several candidates: the source commit distinguishes them.

docs.title: Build the strategic tree
docs.text:
Open Rebalance → Targets. In an older workspace, review the preview for enabling strategic allocation before saving. The app preserves legacy target cells; it does not infer a global plan from current market values.

Add categories, save them, then use saved categories as parents. Assign each position to one leaf category. Unassigned positions stay visible. Review and save category edits and position targets separately; Discard changes abandons a draft. Move child categories and positions before deleting their parent.

Category targets are percentages of their parent. A position target is a percentage of its own category. Global targets multiply these fractions. For example, in an invented plan a category targeting 40% of the portfolio and a position targeting 25% within it imply a 10% portfolio target. Required sibling targets must be complete and sum to 100%; the app does not silently normalize saved targets. Blank means unknown, while zero is an explicit target.

Synthetic offline example: 60% for Equities × 70% for its World ETF gives a 42% portfolio target. The two grids use different denominators. Save categories and Save position targets commit their respective edits separately. These percentages illustrate the controls, not a recommended allocation. Open the image for detail.

Moving a position preserves its within-category target. Check the destination's total after moving it. Zero-quantity positions can carry nonzero targets for future investments. Empty categories retain their targets without artificial chart area.

docs.title: Read the Overview
docs.text:
Select a category to focus its chart, allocation table and positions. Current and target percentages use the selected category as their denominator. Back, the category selector, or the chart center returns to a parent. Parent rows include descendants: adding parent and child values double-counts them. Missing prices suppress complete percentages; the chart represents known value. Exposure filters and ETF expansion do not alter strategic ownership.

With leverage enabled, Market exposure is the first and default allocation view in Overview. It shows current exposure value, current share, target share and Gap (pp), where positive means overweight (current minus target). Capital allocation remains available with its own capital targets; exposure targets are not cash targets. When no separate exposure policy is saved, Market exposure compares against your existing category and position target percentages. For example, 35% current exposure against a 40% target gives a −5 pp gap. This composition comparison requires no target leverage multiple and does not create target currency amounts or change saved percentages. A separately saved market-exposure policy takes precedence; an equity-only or invalid policy is not replaced by this fallback. Use Edit beside either table heading to edit the percentages used there. Hover over the heading for its measure definition. Exposure targets are a separate policy under Rebalance → Targets → Exposure targets: choose a desired total multiple of portfolio net equity and category composition. Capital targets stay unchanged.

Target amounts always use the saved whole-portfolio policy. Within a selected category, current percentages divide by its current exposure, and target percentages divide by its desired exposure. The Overview gap is the difference between these displayed percentages. Monetary exposure gaps in Rebalance remain target minus current exposure; they are not cash purchase budgets. Signed exposures stay signed, and percentages are unavailable when their total is zero or negative. At a leaf category the comparison shows the category total; exposure targets do not imply individual position targets. A saved equity-only policy is labeled as such and is not compared against the broader Market exposure view. Switching its universe to Total market requires an explicit save in the exposure target editor.

Data-coverage details appear when hovering over category names. Unassigned means no strategic category is assigned; an empty zero-value/zero-exposure row is hidden. Offsetting long and short exposures remain represented even if their net is zero. The Notifications bell beside Portfolio settings holds stale ETF snapshots, manual-price notices, valuation/performance gaps and refresh problems. Tooltips explain metrics and table columns without adding paragraphs to the overview. A dot marks unread notices. Opening the panel marks current notices as seen; new, changed or recurring notices light it again. Seen state is separate per portfolio for the current browser session; notices remain available after reading.

docs.title: Analytical labels are separate
docs.text:
Strategic categories are a non-overlapping ownership tree. Analytical taxonomies can describe several aspects of the same asset, such as sector, theme and geography. Edit classifications.yaml in the private workspace for these labels. Back it up first and preserve asset IDs. An invented example for an instrument whose ID is example-company:

example-company:
  classifications:
    sector:
      - [Industry, Example services]
    theme:
      - [Example theme, Example activity]

Taxonomy names and depths are flexible. An asset assigned to several distinct paths splits its value equally among them; repeated identical paths are ignored. Full paths distinguish identically named nodes under different parents. Missing membership becomes Unclassified. An Assigned here chart leaf preserves value attached directly to an internal node. An empty file mapping {} is valid.

Legacy workspaces without strategic allocation use whole-portfolio position targets in target_allocation. Filtered legacy targets retain their original portfolio basis. Review migration in Targets before relying on category-relative planning. See Exposure for analytical filtering.

docs.title: Analytics and risk
docs.text: Overview Analytics follows the selected strategic category and optional account filter. Position search and Exposure filters do not change that scope. Positions also offers Valuation, Income & fees and Risk views, with definitions and sources under Key metrics. Blank metrics mean unavailable, not zero.

docs.title: Historical risk
docs.text:
Choose Calculate risk. The default is three years against MSCI ACWI Net Return, using direct index levels in the portfolio reporting currency. Net return reinvests dividends after index-assumed withholding tax, without ETF fees or personal taxes. Currency translation does not hedge currency risk. Options offers the benchmark and one-, three- or five-year windows.

Usable cached index history takes priority over switching sources. If direct index history is unavailable or has fewer than 52 weekly returns, the calculation uses the adjusted IUSQ.DE ETF history in the reporting currency. The benchmark label changes to MSCI ACWI · ETF proxy and ETF benchmark fallback appears beside the estimate. Sources are never stitched. Custom benchmark tickers do not fall back automatically. The direct reference is MSCI:892400:NETR.

Coverage and exclusions appear in a compact status beside Details, which contains the sample dates, calculation basis and sources. The correlation heatmap is visible above the holdings risk table; Expand enlarges it and shows full names. Full names remain available on hover in compact mode. Blank cells mean undefined correlation, not zero. Columns controls the table's risk measures. Positions with no defined correlations, such as cash in the reporting currency, are omitted from the heatmap but remain in the risk calculations and holdings table. Foreign-currency cash remains visible when its FX returns vary.

The calculation applies today's weights held constant to historical weekly returns. It is a hypothetical allocation, not your personal historical portfolio return or a forecast. It uses dividend/split-adjusted prices and historical FX to the portfolio reporting currency, selecting the last observation in each completed Friday-ending week. Missing weeks are not filled, and returns do not bridge missing endpoints. All included holdings and the benchmark need at least 52 common weekly returns.

Beta is covariance with the benchmark divided by benchmark variance. Volatility annualizes weekly variation using the square root of 52. Correlation measures co-movement, not the size of a possible loss. Volatility contributions sum to the portfolio estimate; negative contributions can reflect diversification.

Cash in the reporting currency has zero FX returns; foreign cash uses historical FX returns. Manual or unlisted assets without suitable history are excluded. Covered weights are renormalized; missing valuations prevent claiming whole-portfolio coverage. Funds use their own histories, not expanded constituents. Category risk still uses the selected benchmark, even for non-equity categories. Version 0.2.0 also supports actual-account leverage in EUR/USD/GBP with net-equity denominators, as described below. The separate legacy simulation remains EUR-only.

Integrated account risk also shows a covered-holdings estimate when some histories are missing or too short. Covered positions retain their weights against whole-portfolio net equity, including signed futures notionals and debt; these weights are not renormalized. The displayed beta, volatility and correlation omit the excluded positions, whose count appears beside the estimate and names and reasons under Details → Risk coverage & sources. Excluded positions can increase or decrease actual risk. Positive, complete net equity and at least 52 common weekly returns are still required.

When you select a category or filter accounts, the main metrics are Subset beta, Subset volatility (annualized) and benchmark correlation. Ordinary subsets normalize the covered holdings to their own net value, including any selected debt. Unselected debt is not assigned to the subset. For example, a subset worth 20% of portfolio equity with beta 1.5 has standalone beta 1.5 and contributes 0.3 to portfolio beta. The view shows that contribution separately below the main metrics, using whole-portfolio net equity.

Subsets containing futures use their selected funded capital, including cash attributed to the investment and unsettled claims counted once. Signed notional remains the future's risk weight numerator. Missing histories do not shrink this capital base. A bare contract's notional, margin requirement or unsettled gain does not establish a standalone capital base: select its funded investment or include its backing capital. Without a positive, fully valued base, standalone metrics remain unavailable while a supported portfolio beta contribution is still shown. Contributions use the subset's common history sample; comparisons across categories need matching dates and coverage to add up exactly.

For reviewed equivalent equity listings, risk can use another venue's adjusted history when the held listing has fewer than 52 benchmark-matched weekly returns. Vertiv's 49V.DE can use its same-share US listing VRT. Historical FX converts that history into the reporting currency; prices from different listings are never stitched together. Coverage sources identify the substitution. This does not change the held ticker or its current valuation, and does not apply to funds or futures proxies.

docs.title: Valuation, income and costs
docs.text:
Aggregate P/E is sum(value) / sum(value / PE) for covered profitable direct stocks. It excludes nonpositive ratios and fund-reported P/E. Fund ratios remain separate. Monetary fundamentals retain their reported currency.

Annual fund cost estimates multiply current fund value by annual fee rate. Fees are already reflected in fund prices; do not subtract the estimate again from gains. Trailing cash distribution estimates multiply current value by reported yield. They are not forecasts or dividends actually received. Verified accumulating share classes have zero cash yield. Coverage limits every aggregate.

Instrument concentration combines repeated instrument IDs across accounts. Underlying-company concentration depends on ETF coverage and reviewed identities; it is distinct from historical volatility.

docs.title: Sources and fee overrides
docs.text:
Fundamentals and adjusted histories have separate private caches, normally valid for 24 hours, with a 15-minute failed-request cooldown. Explicit refresh retries immediately; failures may retain visibly stale data. Ordinary holdings remain available if analytics fails.

Dated issuer fees match the exact share class; an ETF exposure proxy cannot supply another fund's fee. Provider expense ratios are labeled fallbacks. Maintain fund fee stores a private override with share-class identity, annual rate, source, verification date and accumulation policy. Enter rates as percentages. Verification older than 90 days is flagged; removing an override restores issuer/provider data.

docs.title: Source development
docs.text: This page is for contributors working in a source checkout. Installed-app users can use their shortcut and the in-app controls; Python and uv are not needed. Start with source installation before running these commands.

docs.title: Interface design
docs.text:
The main interface prioritizes quantitative results, exploration and actions. Labels, grouping and consistent controls should make the view understandable without introductory paragraphs or repeated explanations.

  • Keep visible prose minimal. Prefer concise labels and short, contextual status text. Put definitions in tooltips or help popovers, and methodology, assumptions, provenance and extended explanations in expandable details or the user guide. Treat prose as a removal signal during UI review: ordinary screens contain results, controls, short labels and actionable errors, not explanatory sentences. Put necessary explanations behind an explicit help action. Do not add paragraphs, repeated instructions, workflow narration or reassurance below controls or tables.
  • Preserve essential meaning in the main view: selected scope, units, the metric's basis and whether a result is approximate, partial or unavailable. Explanations may be disclosed on demand; material limitations must remain discoverable from a visible status beside the affected result.
  • Use compact, local indicators for routine partial coverage, excluded holdings and cached data. Reserve prominent warning banners for blocking problems or situations requiring timely action. Match color and visual prominence to the importance of the state; ordinary analytical limitations should not dominate the page.
  • Put secondary figures near their primary metric. Consolidate repeated status messages and avoid stacks of captions above or below a result. Keep controls aligned with the section they affect and use space to communicate hierarchy.
  • Preserve established styling and shared components. Improve density, placement and consistency before adding decorative elements, new panels or new navigation.
  • Import review must identify the affected statement, show the specific unresolved source rows locally, and offer a decision for that statement. Do not ask users to certify a batch with a blanket checkbox or infer a problem from an absent tax/fee row. Routine fully reconciled statements should not need manual approval.
  • Keep help and status details accessible by keyboard and touch, with meaningful labels. Color and hover alone must not carry essential information.

Apply these principles across the application, including new features and error states. They govern presentation without weakening calculation or coverage rules.

Apply chart_hover at each Plotly rendering boundary. Curves share a vertical date/value guide and formatted tooltips across the plot area; category and allocation charts retain their meaningful category tooltips. Preserve explicit units, missing values and purpose-built hover content. Pointer movement must not trigger Streamlit reruns. Overview history's value/capital boxes follow the hovered observations and include their dates. The inline gain switches from selected-period gain to total known gain during hover. Any range covering the full holding history uses the shared total known gain calculation, just like All. Personal and price histories use currency symbols consistently in summaries, axes and tooltips. Leaving restores the latest value and period gain. Clicking the gain badge toggles between amount and cumulative TWR; its metric name and period appear only in a concise tooltip. Return percentages use ↑/↓; monetary gains keep +/− signs. Zero and unavailable returns have no direction arrow. TWR defaults to the documented daily flow convention; no remaining-cost denominator is substituted. Exact event TWR remains explicit. Annualized money-weighted return always uses full recorded history, independently of the chart range or pointer. Keep one summary row below the view tabs. The allocation measure switch belongs above the allocation table, aligned with its left edge and the top of the chart. Performance keeps category comparison visible and leaves detailed category and position lists to their existing views.

docs.title: View changes and progressive disclosure
docs.text:
Related views must share card widths, minimum heights and alignment. Keep their navigation and outer container stable. Position detail dialogs keep a viewport-bounded height across views and loading states; long content scrolls inside the window. Test the outer bounds throughout transitions, not just card dimensions. Replace the outgoing content before doing expensive work for the next view. Do not calculate a complete history merely to choose an already-selected tab, or repeat calculations during the same render. Reuse chart results only while journal facts, observation revisions, scope, currency, period and calendar date remain unchanged. Within and across chart ranges, share dated ledger states and previously calculated hover results without relaxing coverage checks. Keep this context session-local and expire it when workspace, journal, observations, reporting currency or calendar date changes. Fixed position headlines request only full-history summary results; they do not generate chart points. The Overview history chart, current-gain summary and category comparison share one calculation context for the same journal and observation snapshot. Current quotes remain separate from dated historical valuations. Recorded cost and cash components may be reused between transaction/fee dates; daily prices and reporting FX still resolve at the requested date. A new observation revision creates a new context, including when it arrives in a background fragment. Account history derives securities cash postings once per journal snapshot and reuses account states between cash/account event dates. A settlement value date alone does not release a pending receipt; explicit receipt events remain authoritative. Background data refreshes must remain local to the affected result. Dialog polling fragments must stop writing when their captured position or view is no longer selected; a stale timer must not draw into a replacement view. Verify actual transitions with delayed synthetic data: settled screenshots alone miss old controls and charts briefly appearing during a switch. An explicit retry rebuilds the owning dialog's download state and polling timer; successful completion must update the chart without changing its period or leaving the view. Idle polling checks the observation-file identity before parsing it again, while externally saved corrections still invalidate results.

Position opening and clean dismissal rerun only the dialog host. Creating or discarding an unsaved editor draft refreshes the parent toolbar once so its resume action matches the retained draft. Child workflows share a local refresh boundary, including evidence saves, reconciliation, market evidence repairs and balance review. Persisted changes refresh current position values locally and refresh the parent page once after dismissal. Pending evidence alone does not repeat portfolio valuation. Streamlit 1.65 or newer is required for the keyed host callbacks; the runtime adapter is isolated in dialog_runtime.py and covered by browser lifecycle tests. Transaction list, import, edit and reconciliation screens use distinct keyed containers so their action rows are replaced together. Never leave list actions alongside review/apply controls. Evidence saves retain revision guards and leave balances unchanged until explicitly applied. Position detail tabs always use History, Key metrics, Transactions and Details. Without recorded history evidence, History shows the price chart directly. Otherwise it contains a Holdings / Price selector, defaulting to Holdings when useful holdings history exists and Price otherwise. Remember an explicit choice per position for the session, separately from the editor draft; clear these preferences when switching workspaces. Switching history type keeps the dialog and selector stable and replaces only the result beneath them. Position details keep one shared summary row above the chart selector: Position value with supported personal gain, Invested capital, and Annualized return. These figures retain their current/all-history basis across tabs, chart types, periods and pointer movement. Dated value, capital, total gain and TWR remain in chart tooltips; position charts do not rewrite headline cards. Return on cost and unrealized gain are listed in Details. Without applied history, capital uses the recorded acquisition cost and gain is explicitly unrealized only; annualized return remains unavailable. Applied history supplies the authoritative balance; missing evidence limits only the metrics that depend on it.

Missing-data interfaces must identify the affected result and provide a relevant action. Do not expose a combined list of every metric's requirements as mandatory setup. Keep ordinary gaps subtle. Retrieve supported market data automatically; manual repair forms should preselect the position, date and currencies when known. Internal identities and fingerprints are storage details, not user-facing labels. Never display transaction references, transaction IDs or hash-based IDs in normal product UI: tables, selectors, labels, tooltips, notifications and errors must use readable names and transaction facts instead. If internal identifiers are needed for debugging, expose them only inside an explicitly opened internal diagnostics view, never in the normal import or transaction-review workflow. Show overwrite confirmation only when a value will actually be replaced.

For a single holding, use Apply history after reconciliation. For multiple holdings, review each with Accept this holding, then Apply reviewed holdings in one atomic save. Changes to reviewed facts reset these balance-review decisions. Applying makes the selected ledger authoritative for the resulting holdings, including when it replaces a different current balance. There is no separate history-completeness confirmation, expiry date, or incomplete-apply mode. Return CSV imports to Positions without opening an arbitrary holding. Missing amounts, prices, FX, starting balances and unresolved transactions remain metric-specific limitations. Do not infer evidence before a starting snapshot or claim that applied records prove the absence of omitted real-world transactions. Legacy completeness records remain readable but do not gate results. Market-data correction stays separate from transaction reconciliation.

docs.title: Architecture and verification
docs.text:
Business logic is independent of Streamlit:

holdings → reporting-currency valuation → normalized exposures → optional ETF expansion → classifications
         → hierarchical aggregation → charts and tables

Position filters run after valuation and before exposure normalization. The exposure table retains asset IDs and source-position metadata through ETF expansion. Provider parsing and refresh code are separate from the generic ETF transformation and aggregation engine. All chart types share the same aggregation engine. exposure_analysis.py owns source selection and normalized ETF expansion without Streamlit; the UI supplies selections and renders the resulting tables. currencies.py shares quote-subunit normalization across spot and historical prices.

application.py selects price/FX services, checks leverage eligibility and prepares valuation diagnostics without Streamlit. input_cache.py returns named PortfolioInputs and copies cached inputs before handing them to calculations. ui.py owns workspace recovery, widget interactions, explicit refresh requests and lazy view dispatch. Optional fundamentals and risk remain in analytics_service.py; opening an unrelated view must not fetch them.

Actual accounts join the same pipeline at the reporting-currency valuation boundary. account_journal.py replays native Decimal cash, explicit loans, futures lots and pending claims. actual_portfolio.py projects these into valued rows, replacing adopted cash holdings and retaining position/account provenance. portfolio_exposure.py then uses separate capital and signed-exposure measures; provider parsing and journal persistence do not belong in the aggregation engine.

monitoring.py owns indicator and account-rule calculations; monitoring_market.py normalizes provider observations, monitoring_service.py schedules checks while a session is open, and monitoring_store.py persists rule revisions and alert episodes under the workspace lock. Monitoring does not change holdings or orders. tour_monitoring.py creates its example only after verifying the active tour-owned synthetic directory; it reuses the normal alert explanation and acknowledgment UI.

docs.title: Calculation contracts
docs.text:
Account history advances the canonical replay engine through dated checkpoints, retaining at most 128 in its local timeline. Movement prefixes share an append-only log without changing earlier states. A dated query and complete-journal validation remain distinct: final adoption checks run only when requesting the complete state, and validation failures remain failures on retry. Explicit zero inception uses a validated zero-opening source marker; snapshots never imply unknown prehistory was empty.

Long XIRR schedules can certify uniqueness by enclosing a sign-changing root and all proper discounted cash-flow prefixes with directed decimal intervals. A uniform prefix sign implies the quotient after removing that root has uniformly signed coefficients, hence no other positive roots. Otherwise the solver isolates stationary points after exponential differentiation at a coefficient sign boundary. Work and depth limits produce a separate computational diagnostic; accepted rates still require residual and conditioning checks against the original full schedule.

CSV and PDF readers normalize evidence into the ordinary securities history. Transaction commands, corrections, removals, reconciliation and calculation eligibility depend on economic facts, never the entry source. Linked exchanges, transfers and asset fees are reviewed and applied together. Source references and replacement chains remain immutable provenance; identical reimports cannot undo a later edit or removal. Similar cross-source trades require explicit review.

The small public CSV uses dates and stable references. File order supplies the initial same-day order, which can be overridden with order and edited in the normal transaction form. No execution timestamp is invented. Legacy CSV v1/v2 receipts and journal v1–v4 remain readable. Journal v5 supports independently identified corrections of imported events and transaction estimate qualifiers; simple CSV receipts store sparse normalized facts. Loading older records does not rewrite them or invalidate existing review fingerprints.

New-position identities are staged until application. history_publication.py protects the holdings/journal pair with a durable private recovery intent and revision guards under the workspace lock. Interrupted publications roll back before the next workspace access; unexpected third-party edits stop recovery. Evidence-only saves leave portfolio balances unchanged.

There is one history calculation path: forward holdings, daily TWR and annualized XIRR. Supplied estimates qualify dependent results rather than blocking them. Unknown amounts, missing prices/FX and incomplete transaction coverage remain separate limitations. Acquisition-cost estimates alone do not qualify percentage returns that do not depend on those costs. Legacy asset-performance.json files are preserved as inert private artifacts and do not control views or calculations.

  • gain_accounting.py supplies shared current and historical known-gain results. Security-only and account-only cash flows cancel across their common boundary; account equity includes actual futures once, not their display allocation again. Result coverage and valuation provenance are separate from amounts. Historical acquisition capital and return-opening market value are distinct. Summary-only and snapshot fallbacks remain explicit, and missing return evidence never shortens All. Historical renderers consume calculated gains/TWR in customdata; browser code formats them but does not reconstruct financial calculations.

  • Saved positions retain their instrument ID and stable position ID. A contribution has an analytical asset ID plus its source position/instrument identity; company grouping must not overwrite the original security identity.

  • exposures.project_contributions accepts an explicitly aligned measure and copies source dimensions. Current value, target fractions and performance amounts can use the same transformation without pretending to be the same financial measure. Reserved calculation columns are rejected as custom CSV metadata. New calculated fields must extend that reservation.
  • constituents.py interprets normalized constituent facts. Each consumer owns its coverage policy: an equity fund's residual can be equity exposure while remaining unresolved company exposure. Futures proxy coverage also retains its stricter treatment of unidentified and non-equity weights.
  • Actual contract facts use derivative_types.py; account_journal.py owns signed lot arithmetic, FIFO reductions, settlements and native postings. Settled P&L is already cash; only unsettled P&L and pending claims add derivative wealth. Notional is exposure, never wealth. Security collateral is a quantity reservation against an existing holding, not another asset.
  • account_observations.py and derivative_market.py keep dated marks and free exact-contract observations separate from cash postings. account_margin.py evaluates entered requirements and haircuts without inferring broker rules. eurex_quotes.py isolates the anonymous public quote protocol and exact monthly contract validation. futures_quotes.py retains automatic observations and refresh status separately from manual marks and the journal; futures_valuation.py selects absolute prices and derives local freshness. Quote timestamps and retrieval timestamps must remain distinct. Settlement reference time orders valuations; it is not a fabricated quote/publication time. Daily cash eligibility uses Europe/Berlin business dates, independent of whether the archive changed since the last worker run. account_planning.py previews integer trades without changing account facts.
  • FuturePosition and future_projections.py retain the legacy EUR sandbox's funded-strategy arithmetic and named capital, exposure and risk adapters. Legacy simulation value must not enter actual account projections.
  • generalized_studies.py consumes copied scenario inputs, native price paths and explicit FX, margin, rate and transfer assumptions. Its results never write the account journal. study_market.py validates history identity, currency and return convention before a proxy can drive a reconstruction.
  • Missing amounts are not zero. Callers retain completeness information when projecting known contributions. prepare_market_analysis returns separate known-value chart nodes and completeness-preserving table nodes. Composition percentages use selected exposure; portfolio impact uses whole-portfolio equity.

Preparation results own their output frames; frozen result containers do not make pandas frames deeply immutable. Treat inputs as borrowed, copy before mutation, and verify conservation, source provenance and input nonmutation when changing these boundaries. company_analysis.py prepares company grouping and coverage; renderers consume the prepared results.

docs.title: Session lifetimes
docs.text:
state_lifecycle.py is the single catalog of feature-owned navigation, workspace, currency and tour policies. Add an ordinary widget input to its feature's declaration, with the correct mount boundary. Inputs may survive lazy unmounts and are restored once on remount so the browser receives the retained value. Remount bookkeeping is consumed only after view dispatch, preserving it across early-return dialogs. Buttons, upload handles and editor patches must not be reassigned as ordinary input state. Imports and persistent editors keep their specialized adapters. Registered ordinary import review controls also use the Positions/Import remount boundary so a delayed navigation request cannot leave their browser value at its default while the backend retains the reviewed choice. The holdings uploader discards stale widget handles on that return while retaining the draft file bytes; explicitly removing an uploaded file still clears its retained selection. Calculation fingerprints stay with the calculators that understand their assumptions.

Currency changes clear monetary drafts and prior monetary plans while retaining scope and percentage preferences. Workspace changes clear owned drafts/results; workspace-keyed analytics preferences remain isolated by their keys. Tour capture copies only declared restorable state. Exercise real navigation as well as pure transition tests, including date controls and nested lazy views.

Document writes retain their workspace locking, revision checks and backup policies. Commands validating multiple documents must hold the workspace lock from validation through publication. Cache and document writers deliberately retain different failure/recovery policies; sharing serialization mechanics must not erase those differences. atomic_file.staged_text only creates and cleans up a same-directory text stage, optionally flushing and syncing its content. Callers choose serialization, locks, backups and revision checks, then explicitly replace the destination. Document writers sync before backing up and rechecking revisions; cache writers preserve their own validation and failure fallback. ETF snapshot publication still writes the manifest last; it is a separate multi-file protocol.

money.py formats scalar amounts with explicit currency and no Streamlit state. currency_display.py supplies session reporting units and numeric formats for native grids. Actual account entries retain EUR/USD/GBP units; projections perform explicit conversion before display. Only legacy fixed-EUR sandbox views use money.euros; formatting never converts amounts. Missing values remain missing. Shared list columns retain numeric sorting and their browser formatter. charts.chart_config provides compact allocation controls and explicit zoom/pan/reset controls for scenario studies; each chart receives independent configuration containers.

uv run pytest
uv run portfolio-app --demo --server.headless=true

Table editors stay attached to their cells while scrolling. While editing, Tab saves and opens the next editable field; Shift+Tab moves back. Escape cancels the current edit. Enter edits a selected cell or toggles a selected checkbox.

Optional browser regressions exercise these interactions in an isolated, synthetic Streamlit app. Install Chromium with uv run --with playwright playwright install chromium, then run uv run --with playwright pytest tests/test_grid_browser.py.

Tests use generated synthetic fixtures, injected prices, FX, search responses, and clocks, with no live network required. Importer coverage uses independently authored positioned-cell and text-stream PDF layouts in tests/consors_audit_fixtures.py, alongside the original fixtures. Expected quantities, charges, FIFO costs and proceeds are explicit constants, not calculated by parser helpers. Public format references inform labels and layout only; all fixture identities, dates and financial values are invented. Equivalent layout variants must preserve event economics, while unsupported or ambiguous fields must remain blocked even when totals happen to balance. The importer audit tests also cover retained evidence versus activation, revision/duplicate guards, page/row provenance and masked-output sentinels.

They cover valuation, persistent cache fallback, parent/child conservation, multi-path classifications, filtering, denominators, targets, ETF residuals, company exposure merging, snapshot refresh failure recovery, position saves, backups, stale-edit rejection, bulk purchase averaging and historical cost entry, listing search, minimum-trade and minimum-cash rebalancing, trade-count tradeoffs, empty-position redistribution, Git privacy guards, and Streamlit controls. The server health endpoint is /_stcore/health.

Independent target overrides on analytical-taxonomy nodes, ordinary-security tax reporting and automatic broker transaction imports remain unsupported. The account journal records actual futures settlements and closes; an opening snapshot does not reconstruct pre-snapshot gains. Strategic category targets, instrument price history and historical risk analysis are supported.

docs.title: Shared list presentation
docs.text:
src/portfolio_app/list_ui.py defines the shared read-only list component, column formatting, taxonomy badges, sorting, row actions and scrolling policy. Overview allocations/performance, position lists, Exposure assets and source contributions, ETF constituent lists, and Suggested trades use it. Keep presentation changes here instead of copying table CSS or row-selection controls into individual pages. Use ListColumn for column labels, numeric precision and signed values.

Lists grow with the page by default. Exposure enables the shared BOUNDED_LIST_HEIGHT only when ETF breakdown is enabled; ETF constituent details also use that limit. Narrow screens retain horizontal scrolling. Editable spreadsheet forms and analytical diagnostic tables retain their native grid controls. Search within a displayed list does not recalculate allocation weights.

Exposure's main list shows how many source positions contribute to each asset. Opening an asset shows each direct or ETF position's reporting-currency contribution and its percentage of that asset's exposure, with separate account positions preserved. Missing source valuations leave contribution percentages unavailable.

docs.title: Parallel development
docs.text: Use a separate Git worktree and branch for each coding session, with one session responsible for integrating shared UI changes. Run each demo on a different port and use generated synthetic data. Personal data and the private handoff remain outside Git. In a source checkout, use docs/release-plan.md for the reusable release procedure, docs/release-checklist.md for acceptance criteria, and these behavior/reference guides for product context. Tests and demos must not read private working data. Run uv run pytest after integration. Browser checks are optional locally: uv run --with playwright pytest tests/test_ux_browser.py tests/test_dashboard_browser.py. Set PORTFOLIO_TEST_CHROMIUM to an available Chromium binary if needed.

docs.title: Analytics development notes
docs.text: These implementation notes are also published with the guide. See the task guides for application usage and formulas, and contributor instructions for privacy and development requirements. These notes contain no working portfolio data.

docs.title: Current product state
docs.text:
• Navigation follows the UI refactor: Overview, Exposure, Positions, Rebalance.
  • Overview → Analytics shares the existing category selection, including its descendants. Accounts can be narrowed in Options. Exposure filters and position search do not change this scope.
  • Historical risk comes first. Calculate risk loads the estimates; subsequent refreshes are explicit. Benchmark and history window are in Options.
  • Risk shows beta, annualized volatility, benchmark correlation, per-holding beta and volatility contributions, and data coverage. The expandable correlation matrix uses display names without appended identifiers, a purple–teal diverging scale fixed at −1 to +1, a nearby color bar, and a larger responsive plot.
  • Valuation and income follow risk. Direct-stock P/E excludes ETFs and nonpositive ratios. Fund fees and cash distribution yields do include eligible ETFs. Concentration and underlying company exposure are separate views of risk.
  • Positions has Holdings, Valuation, Income & fees, and Risk views. Optional columns and settings live in Options. Selecting a row opens its existing details dialog; Key metrics contains fundamentals, definitions, provenance, and a private fund-fee editor. Holdings does not request analytics data.
  • Preserve the refactor's shared table interactions, short names, search, sort, keyboard access, row details, and separate pencil editing when extending views.

docs.title: Calculation contracts
docs.text:
• Snapshot weights use current reporting-currency market values and combine repeated instrument IDs across accounts. Buy-in performance belongs to Overview → Performance.
  • P/E is the inverse of value-weighted earnings yield among covered profitable direct equities. It is not an arithmetic average, and fund-reported P/E is not blended into it. Coverage is essential to interpreting this subset statistic.
  • Fees are current fund values × annual fee rates. They are already reflected in prices and must not be deducted from gains a second time. Public fee metadata is matched by exact share class, not an ETF look-through proxy.
  • Cash yield is a trailing distribution estimate, not a forecast or actual dividends received. Verified accumulating share classes have zero cash yield.
  • Risk uses adjusted market-price histories, converted with historical FX to the reporting currency. The latest available price within each completed Friday-ending week is used. Empty weeks are not filled, and returns do not bridge missing endpoints.
  • Default benchmark is the direct MSCI ACWI net-return index (892400, NETR), requested in reporting currency and validated against returned metadata. Usable cached index levels precede a disclosed IUSQ.DE fallback. Custom tickers do not substitute automatically; neither index nor equity histories are stitched. Windows are 1, 3, or 5 years, default 3. All included holdings and the benchmark share the same sample of at least 52 weekly returns. Provider-supplied betas are not used.
  • Portfolio weekly return is the sum of holding weekly returns × today's weights. Beta is covariance with the benchmark / benchmark variance. Annualized covariance is weekly covariance × 52. Contributions to volatility sum to portfolio volatility; negative contributions are possible.
  • This is a hypothetical constant-weight allocation, not the user's historical return series. It requires no transaction history and does not use buy-in prices.
  • Cash in the reporting currency has zero FX returns. In ordinary asset analysis, manual/unlisted positions without supported history are excluded, covered weights are renormalized, and partial coverage is shown. Missing valuations prevent claiming whole-portfolio coverage. Integrated account leverage shows a labelled covered-holdings estimate with exclusions and fixed whole-portfolio net-equity weights; missing histories do not suppress otherwise usable metrics. Missing/nonpositive net equity or an insufficient common sample still prevents an estimate. Reviewed same-share equity history fallbacks are currency-converted independently and disclosed; valuation tickers and futures proxies stay separate.
  • ETFs use their own adjusted price histories for risk, not constituent expansion. Category/account subsets show standalone beta and volatility on selected capital, with portfolio beta contribution secondary. Ordinary subsets normalize covered net funded values; derivative subsets require positive, fully valued selected backing capital. Count unsettled claims once before adding risk-only FX rows; never use margin or bare-contract gains as capital. A missing subset base does not suppress an otherwise supported portfolio beta contribution. The benchmark remains selected even for non-equity categories. Subset and contribution metrics use the same sample, which can differ across categories.
  • Ordinary holdings use asset-normalized beta. Version 0.2.0 also supports actual-account leverage in EUR/USD/GBP, with a separate net-equity denominator. Asset-normalized beta must not be presented as levered equity beta; legacy sandbox risk remains EUR-only.
  • Actual futures risk uses signed notional with compatible contract-currency histories and converts native changes at dated FX. It must not apply the FX return on the whole futures notional. Foreign cash, claims and debt carry their own FX risk. A documented leveraged ETF factor changes current exposure; risk still uses that fund's own price returns without multiplying leverage twice.

docs.title: Code map
docs.text:
Module Responsibility fundamentals.py Metric definitions, provider normalization, dated public fees, private overrides analytics_cache.py Atomic optional-analytics cache, expiry, failed-request cooldown analytics.py Pure snapshot aggregation and concentration risk_data.py Adjusted price histories and historical reporting-currency conversion risk.py Pure common-sample weekly risk calculations analytics_service.py Provider/cache orchestration for fundamentals and risk, independent of Streamlit company_analysis.py Pure company grouping and exposure preparation, plus workspace mapping loading analytics_ui.py Shared formatting, sources, benchmark settings portfolio_analytics_ui.py Overview analytics presentation position_metrics_ui.py Position metric presets, details, fee maintenance charts.py → correlation_chart Correlation matrix rendering position_list.py, position_detail.py, strategic_ui.py Integration with the existing UX

Keep analytics outside the holdings → valuation → optional ETF expansion → normalized exposures → classifications → aggregation pipeline. Reuse the valued positions already prepared by the app instead of fetching valuations again. Company concentration reuses the existing company mapping and ETF exposure logic.

Analytics caches are private and separate from the ordinary price/chart caches. Their normal lifetime is 24 hours; failed requests have a 15-minute cooldown. Failures can retain visibly stale data. Explicit refresh retries immediately. Fee overrides are private fund-fees.json data. Do not commit overrides, caches, test screenshots, diagnostics, or real portfolio examples. Only explicitly reviewed synthetic guide images may enter the public documentation.

docs.title: Potential extensions and decisions to make first
docs.text:
These are ideas, not promises or already implemented features.

  1. Compare categories side by side. Show beta, volatility, value share, and coverage for sibling categories. Decide whether all categories must share a single common sample; independently estimated betas are less comparable. Distinguish category beta from its contribution to whole-portfolio beta.
  2. Current versus proposed allocation. Preview hypothetical target weights with beta, volatility, concentration, and coverage. Reuse a single historical sample and covariance matrix for both scenarios. Decide how this connects to Rebalance and how infeasible targets or missing histories are displayed.
  3. Beta stability. Add rolling beta or comparisons across windows, confidence intervals, and benchmark explanatory power. A point estimate alone should not imply a stable forecast. Do not confuse beta with total volatility.
  4. Joint funded-asset and futures planning. The app already provides actual-account futures plans alongside the capital planner. Joint routing between funded holdings and derivatives would need explicit funding, transfer and financing assumptions. A leveraged ETF's advertised daily multiple is neither a guaranteed multiyear return multiple nor its beta against an arbitrary benchmark.
  5. Downside scenarios. Separate simple beta-based shocks from historical constant-weight scenarios. Neither reconstructs personal performance or sets a worst-case loss bound. Define treatment of missing assets and costs first.
  6. Fund valuation coverage. Keep fund-reported P/E separate for now. Combining direct stocks and look-through fund earnings requires compatible earnings, dates, loss treatment, and coverage; do not silently average unlike ratios.
  7. Metric loading UX. Risk currently needs Calculate risk; fundamentals load when Analytics is selected. Decide whether to load risk automatically, retain results across scope changes, or add progress/background loading. Preserve clear freshness and partial-data reporting and avoid repeated network requests.
  8. Benchmark presets and persistence. Currently a ticker field and a shared benchmark per analytics view. Category-specific defaults, saved preferences, or named presets would require explicit scope and persistence choices.
  9. Large heatmaps. Consider top-N selection, ordering/clustering, and duplicate display-name disambiguation without reintroducing noisy ticker suffixes. Numeric axis coordinates already preserve distinct cells for duplicate names.

docs.title: Validation and resuming work
docs.text:
Use uv run pytest. Focused analytics tests are tests/test_analytics.py, tests/test_risk.py, and tests/test_analytics_ui.py. Browser coverage is in tests/test_analytics_browser.py, with shared synthetic fixtures from tests/test_ux_browser.py. Tests must never read the working portfolio or require live market-data access. Browser-test screenshots remain in temporary directories; the separate guide-image capture/review procedure is in docs/documentation-maintenance.md in the source checkout.

Run checks against the exact intended source commit. Previous test counts and another checkout's running preview do not establish that the current app works. Use a separate linked worktree per task and preserve other sessions' changes.

For a separate preview:

uv run portfolio-app --data-dir /path/to/synthetic-workspace --server.port 8502 --server.runOnSave true

Use a generated synthetic workspace explicitly when launching from a worktree. Restart that preview if imported modules remain stale; do not restart another session's app. Check the port before assuming which version a browser tab displays.

docs.title: Browser acceptance
docs.text:
Use synthetic workspaces and preserve observable value, persistence and lifecycle assertions. Streamlit's idle script marker can still describe the previous render while a widget update is queued. Commit dependent text edits one at a time and await the corresponding request and successful render before editing the next field. A received protocol message alone does not establish that React has painted. Wait for finite layout animations before targeting controls inside expanders; infinite decorative animations must not block readiness.

Use browser_runtime.browser_session() and start_server() for synthetic browser tests. The session pool reuses Chromium processes while closing every context between tests and recycling each process after eight uses to bound retained trace storage; workspaces, ports and Streamlit processes remain test-owned. Use browser_support.open_app() to install the protocol observer before navigation, then await the initial connection, acknowledged rerun and settled render. Use select_tab() for ordinary fixture navigation. Keep intentional race tests explicit. Pure protocol state-machine cases belong in test_browser_protocol.py so they run without launching a browser.

Set PORTFOLIO_BROWSER_EVIDENCE to an external or ignored directory to retain setup, call and teardown failures. Evidence is staged before resources close and discarded for passing tests. It includes synthetic server logs, Playwright traces, screenshots, HTML and bounded protocol lifecycle events. Never use this harness against a personal workspace. See docs/release-plan.md in the source checkout for selected node IDs, explicit repetitions and packaged-stage commands.

Capture failure evidence while the browser and page are still alive. Inspect the first failure before retrying; additional clicks, longer timeouts or removed assertions do not establish a correct interaction. Candidate builds run the source application smoke before the full suite so basic workflow failures surface early.

docs.title: Before committing
docs.text:
Keep the pre-commit hook enabled, run uv run portfolio-check-private --staged, and inspect the staged diff. Never commit private holdings or portfolio exports.

Background market, monitoring and settlement collection continues while a position dialog is open. Defer automatic full-page refreshes until it closes; chart-history completion renders inside its local fragment. User-requested saves still revalidate revisions and refresh portfolio balances.

Settlement polling compares selected valuation inputs and journal changes rather than cache modification times. Starting collection, downloading the same quote, and crossing a wall-clock minute do not rerun the application. Source-check notices update within Notifications. Freshness regions age the displayed snapshot without rereading prices or recalculating holdings/history: metrics, position rows and category-comparison qualification stay current while navigation and editors remain mounted. The list component patches freshness metadata in place to retain focus, sorting, scroll and expanded details. Material data changes still revalue the portfolio together, deferred while a position dialog is open.

docs.title: Optional transaction history
docs.text:
security_history.py owns fractional Decimal holdings, FIFO cost components, opening boundaries and retained evidence. history_commands.py coordinates reviewed activation with workspace locks and revision guards. Activated holdings are materialized before valuation; their CSV source balances are not independently updated. Securities cash postings are generated into account replay and are never stored as duplicate account events. Futures arithmetic remains in its existing replay branches. Incomplete cash amounts carry an explicit unknown-balance mask.

FIFO lot partitions must conserve component shares, original costs and supplied converted costs. Calculate the disposed portion once and derive its remainder; do not independently scale both sides with a rounded ratio. Quantity validation remains exact, including when a derived lot is reloaded at another Decimal precision.

history_observations.py stores dated observations and retains legacy scope reviews. personal_performance.py computes equity, external flows, money-weighted returns and daily/exact time-weighted returns without Streamlit or network calls. personal_market.py supplies provider observations with explicit adjustment semantics. history_ui.py renders the optional workflows. Keep source-position history separate from present-day ETF constituent expansion and hypothetical risk backtests. Applying history establishes the ledger used for the resulting position; new market data never changes its transactions.

History charts share a HistoryCalculation for one journal and observation revision. SecurityTimeline advances the canonical FIFO replay once and retains dated snapshots for out-of-order range queries. Separately dated charges must keep their own cash dates; failed advances must preserve earlier snapshots. Reuse selected events and cash flows across price-only dates, while retaining exact interval starts for account-opening flows. Immutable observation files are parsed once per exact byte version in a bounded cache. Financial evidence, coverage checks and unknown amounts must remain identical to fresh calculations. Category comparisons request TWR without computing unused annualized returns. XIRR may reverse its discount polynomial to shorten derivative isolation, but must still isolate all positive roots and verify the returned rate against the original cash-flow schedule.

Performance checks must include a fresh browser session after a server restart, as well as interval switches. A warm session cache does not establish acceptable initial-load performance. Use synthetic ledgers for repeatable regression checks; read-only inspection of a running portfolio must emit only timing metadata.

docs.title: History playground
docs.text:
Create a separate, persistent example with invented holdings, buys, a sale, a distribution, fees and cash contributions and withdrawals. --market-prices downloads actual Yahoo Finance closing prices; omit it for deterministic invented prices in offline tests. Invented trade dates use observed market sessions. This reads no user portfolio and refuses to overwrite a nonempty directory:

uv run python -m portfolio_app.demo_history /tmp/portfolio-history-demo --market-prices
uv run streamlit run src/portfolio_app/ui.py --server.port=8527 -- --data-dir /tmp/portfolio-history-demo --demo --ignore-workspace-selection --skip-intro

This direct Streamlit launch uses the prepared history directory; the normal portfolio-app --demo launcher creates its own fresh demonstration data. Choose a free port and keep the playground separate from other sessions. Restarting this command retains edits; generating another example requires a new, empty directory.

Open Overview → Performance for total value, opening capital plus net contributions, investment gain, annualized money-weighted return across all recorded history. Positions with useful history open directly on the History tab. The playground opens portfolio Performance by default. Both views use periods ending today. Edit transaction opens the individual transaction form.

The demo includes exact flow-boundary observations for the portfolio and the fee-free money-market holding. The equity holding has a money-weighted return; daily TWR includes its recorded fees; exact event TWR additionally needs supported event boundaries. Applying edited financial history recalculates affected results.

docs.title: Transaction CSV boundary
docs.text:
transaction_csv.py parses textual CSV facts and retains original evidence without market access. csv_transaction_imports.py prepares a pure batch reconstruction; transaction_import_commands.py revalidates revisions under the workspace lock and publishes positions and history together with recoverable publication. The interface renders the same preview that the save command recomputes.

Journal version 5 retains import provenance, correction lineage and void records. Older journals retain their semantics and remain readable. New position identities and listing connections remain staged until application; publication recovers as one holdings/history pair, never partially applied swap or transfer legs. Derived cash postings remain unpersisted, and custody identity is separate from cash ownership.

Security replay owns non-cash swaps, in-kind income and asset fees alongside existing FIFO history. Lot splits multiply before dividing to avoid avoidable intermediate rounding; imported lot ordering retains execution time and explicit ties. Monetary gain components distinguish analytical swap proceeds from purchase payments and sale cash receipts. Scope calculations cancel internal movements before requesting cross-boundary monetary evidence.

docs.title: Read direct and indirect exposure
docs.text:
In Exposure, Assets combines direct holdings and fund-derived exposure. Break down ETFs starts enabled; supported funds start selected. Use Individual ETFs under Data & settings to keep a specific fund whole. Unsupported, missing or disabled breakdowns remain whole instruments. Expansion never creates owned positions or changes quantities and strategic categories.

Each constituent contribution equals the fund position's reporting-currency value times the stored constituent weight. Matching identities combine direct and indirect value; source details preserve account and portfolio contributions. Source-position filters apply before expansion. Search hides resulting assets without changing the selected source scope's percentage denominator. Hierarchy navigation drills into the resulting allocations. Missing source valuations keep full-selection percentages unavailable.

Classifications use local taxonomy paths, with provider metadata as fallback. Unclassified is a lack of labels, not a missing price. Company-country geography is not revenue exposure; listing currency, exchange and fund domicile are not substitutes. Unknown geography and coverage remain visible. The stock-only view excludes non-equity sources and reports unresolved coverage separately.

The Sector view distinguishes No business sector from Unclassified. Explicitly identified money-market exposure, gold, crypto and cash appear under the former, with separate subcategories. They remain in the portfolio denominator. Unknown company sectors, unsupported fund breakdowns and uncovered ETF weights remain Unclassified. Saved sector labels and provider sectors take precedence; custom themes are not automatically assigned.

docs.title: Futures and exposure measures
docs.text:
With futures or leverage enabled, Exposure opens the same Assets table with Market exposure selected. Contributions from direct holdings, ETFs and futures proxies combine under the same company. Expand Sources to distinguish those channels; details retain proxy dates, methods and unresolved weights. Proxy composition is approximate, not a claim to own the index constituents.

% of selected exposure uses the signed exposure of the selected source scope. % of portfolio equity uses whole-portfolio net equity and can exceed 100%. Cash contributes to equity but has zero market exposure. Shorts remain negative; nonpositive or incomplete denominators make composition percentages unavailable. Charts use signed bars where an area chart would obscure negative contributions.

Under Data & settings, Analysis measure → Funded value uses the same controls to inspect funded holdings, cash and claims. Futures capital remains at source level rather than being attributed to proxy companies. Notional never becomes wealth, a gain or a purchase budget. Ordinary portfolios without leverage retain their existing funded look-through presentation.

Look through funds & futures controls expansion when futures are present. The linked ETF's choice under Individual ETFs also controls its use as a futures composition proxy. A collapsed future retains its full signed exposure. Source filters do not remove the proxy metadata needed to analyze a selected future when its companion ETF is outside the source scope.

Assets opens without a chart. Lists above 200 assets use 100-row pages; sorting, search and percentages use the complete selection. The optional company chart shows at most 30 contributions by absolute amount. Theme charts initially show categories; large individual-asset charts use bounded bars. Detailed provenance, company scenarios and source tables are prepared when opened.

Ordinary equity funds use their current value as the exposure basis, excluding explicit cash. An unsupported constituent type does not invalidate that fund total: its weight stays in Other, with the original security named in provenance. This is unresolved attribution of the fund's exposure, not a computed delta or notional for a right, warrant or other underlying derivative. Explicit leveraged/inverse fund factors take precedence; unknown leverage remains unknown.

When the fund's exposure basis itself is unknown, or valuation is missing, Why is exposure incomplete? identifies the source and constituent. Overview and collapsed fund rows retain Known exposure subtotals; their charts show resolved contributions only. The full total, composition percentages and leverage ratios remain unavailable where they require the unresolved amount. An unknown contribution is never treated as zero or silently reclassified.

docs.title: Understand Other and dates
docs.text:
Constituent weights are fractions of the whole fund. In an invented 80%-covered snapshot, named holdings retain 80% and the remaining 20% stays Other. The app does not scale named constituents to 100%. Other can represent a partial snapshot and is not automatically an error. Check the source interpretation and holdings date before drawing conclusions from a large residual.

To inspect these weights, select an asset in Exposure → Assets, open its details, then expand ETF breakdown and select Holdings.

Synthetic offline example: named constituents cover 98.50% of this invented snapshot; Other retains 1.50%. Fund allocation is a percentage of the whole fund. Selected ETF exposure is the corresponding amount from the selected fund position. These are invented weights, not actual issuer holdings. Open the image for detail.

A source's holdings date differs from a download/check time. Automatic checks normally consider snapshots at least one day old, with one attempt per fund per 24 hours after a successful check. Failed discovery/refresh attempts can retry after five minutes when the app is next used; provider fixes trigger an immediate retry of failures saved by older adapters. Repeated reruns do not repeatedly hit the provider. The threshold can be set from 1–30 days or automatic checks disabled. Refresh ETF holdings now bypasses the throttle. Failed updates retain prior snapshots; a fresh check may return the same old holdings date. Snapshots older than seven days retain a recency notice. Price refresh and ETF refresh are separate. The app must be running for its background checks. While a refresh runs, Notifications shows its progress separately from alerts. Progress does not count as an unread notification; saved snapshots remain usable until the completed update is loaded.

docs.title: Set up and inspect a source
docs.text:
Open Data & settings → ETF refresh & snapshots for status, source links and saved snapshots. Select an asset for its contributing positions and ETF breakdown. Automatic discovery covers supported physical equity/bond products from official iShares, Xtrackers, Amundi, Vanguard and State Street/SPDR feeds, plus reviewed overnight-rate funds and existing explicit integrations. These are shared provider adapters, not a list of individually configured ETFs. Coverage depends on each provider’s published catalogue, replication method and export format.

ISIN is authoritative; WKN/listing searches need a unique issuer-confirmed match. Use Set up a breakdown with an official iShares, Xtrackers, Amundi, Vanguard UK professional, or State Street/SPDR product page when automatic discovery cannot resolve it. Names and bare tickers are insufficient. Bare SMH is the US-listed fund, not a UCITS listing. The verified Xetra listings EXS1.DE (DAX) and EUNA.DE (Global Aggregate Bond) are available by ISIN in search even when live search omits the ETF listing.

Amundi uses the exact ISIN in its product API; Vanguard and State Street use issuer catalogues and recheck the share-class identity. Vanguard holdings are collected across all pages before publication. Refresh reconstructs the adapter from the saved product page, so newly discovered funds remain refreshable.

Published whole-fund weights are preserved. When full weights exceed 100% only because of small published rounding, a labeled view of up to ten top holdings keeps the rest in Other. Amundi compositions containing cash borrowing or unsupported security types also use a labeled partial view. No weights are rescaled to hide these limitations. Vanguard derivatives and rights are excluded; short security positions are rejected. Trading-country metadata is not substituted for company country, and missing issuer, currency or rating data remains unknown. Malformed, truncated, mismatched or unsupported exports retain the previous snapshot. A provider name alone does not guarantee support for every strategy.

For Global Aggregate Bond EUR Hedged, iShares publishes many more than ten holdings. The app's top-ten fallback applies when the exported market values do not reconcile with the published whole-fund weights; it is an app limitation, not a claim that the issuer only supplies ten bonds. The rest remains Other.

For a physical fund from another source, supply a normalized UTF-8 CSV, exact fund ISIN, holdings date and asset class. Required columns are constituent_id,name,ticker,isin,weight. Weights use fractions, not percentages. Bond/money-market rows additionally need instrument_type; optional metadata includes issuer, country, market currency, ISO maturity and credit rating. Review identity, coverage and interpretation before Save breakdown. A manual CSV disables provider refresh for that snapshot; saving a reviewed official source re-enables it. Draft uploads remain in memory until saved.

The Amundi Europe Momentum integration is explicitly a same-index iShares proxy, not the actual Amundi holdings or an exact index file. Proxies approximate allocation and must remain labeled. Unverified synthetic compositions stay whole.

docs.title: Bonds and overnight-rate funds
docs.text:
Physical bond funds offer Summary by issuer, country, denomination currency, maturity and credit quality, plus individual securities under Holdings. Different bonds stay distinct from one another and from the issuer's equity. Maturity bands use the snapshot date. Unknown metadata stays unknown. Published aggregate ratings are not assigned to individual bonds. Duration, yield and other provider metrics retain their own dates. Denomination currency does not measure hedged net FX risk.

For iShares Core Global Aggregate Bond EUR Hedged (IE00BDBRDM35), an export that cannot be reconciled as complete falls back to its ten largest published bond positions. Their whole-fund weights are preserved; Other retains the rest. Coverage and partial summaries are labeled explicitly. Missing ISINs use provider-specific identities, without guessing price tickers or merging issuers.

XEON's economic view represents its EUR overnight-rate benchmark. Its actual substitute basket is available separately under Holdings with signed weights; that basket does not enter portfolio company, country or bond allocations. Economic representation and basket coverage are separate. Provider cash netting can form a net liquidity pool without a country/currency assignment; it must not be read as extra equity exposure. Unsupported net borrowing is rejected.

Verified overnight-rate economic exposure is shown separately as Money market in Geography, including when the ETF is shown whole. Substitute-basket countries do not describe this exposure and are excluded.

Amundi Smart Overnight Return uses the same separation: its economic view is EUR overnight-rate exposure to the ESTR Compounded Index, while available top substitute-basket holdings appear separately at their published weights. Basket coverage is partial and never rescaled. This fund's benchmark does not include XEON's +8.5bp spread. A changed provider identity, benchmark, currency or replication method requires review rather than silently changing the economic interpretation.

docs.title: Company ownership
docs.text:
Choose Exposure → Companies for direct shares and supported equity holdings inside funds. No extra Show checkbox is required. Source scope, individual fund choices and company identity rules still apply. Additional category exclusions remove source positions before look-through. Searching the displayed companies does not change percentage denominators.

This is a funded-ownership view: stock-universe percentages include unresolved equity residuals, while portfolio percentages use the selected source scope before the additional exclusions. Unknown totals leave percentages unavailable. Coverage stays beside the results; residuals, sources and identity explanations are expandable. Futures notional is not treated as funded company ownership.

docs.title: Liabilities and leveraged funds
docs.text:
In Rebalance → Targets, legacy EUR workspaces expose Recorded liabilities & leveraged funds. Add or select a liability by name, enter its account/lender and outstanding EUR balance, then save. Blank means unknown; zero means a known zero balance. Editing preserves its identity. Removal requires selecting Remove this liability. Debt adopted into the account journal is managed under Futures → Cash & financing instead.

The same named ETF editor is used for fund factors throughout the app. Select the held fund and optional unlevered reference by name; retain the dated source, signed factor and reset convention. Saved factors whose holdings are unavailable remain visible for review and explicit removal. Other liabilities, factors and target policies are preserved when saving an individual record.

docs.title: Review company merges and display groups
docs.text:
Company merges uses shared security identities and reviewed equivalences. Where identities are missing, estimated normalized full-name matches are marked *; these are not issuer verification. Inspect source names, identifiers, funds, dates and match method. Undo merge keeps a group separate; Restore merge combines it again. Choices are saved privately. Merging values does not change owned positions or multiply exposure by ADR receipt ratios.

The optional Group SMH with related stocks is a display group containing the whole selected UCITS fund and selected direct stocks. It follows the fund's labels; other ETFs can still expand. Effective exposure retains original contributions. This grouping does not change saved holdings, targets or buy-ins.

docs.title: Compare overlapping labels
docs.text: In the label comparison controls, a selected label includes descendants. If an asset matches several selected labels, explicitly choose Split equally or Count in each label. Splitting divides matching value into a 100% allocation; counting includes the full value in each matching label and percentages can total more than 100%. Overlap uses bars rather than a pie/sunburst implying a partition. Coverage identifies value outside the selected labels. AI theme membership indicates a business role, not a measured percentage of company revenue from AI.
