docs.title: Your first portfolio
docs.text: This walkthrough follows the app tour: understand an allocation, look inside funds, inspect positions, try a contribution plan, then explore Monitoring. Afterwards, switch to your own workspace, save a holding and make a backup. If you have not installed the app, start with Install and run.

docs.title: Explore a temporary demo
docs.text:
Launch the installed app from your shortcut and choose Explore demo in the welcome dialog. No terminal, Python or uv is needed. For a guided example that also works without market-data access, choose Take the tour instead.

The header should say Demo portfolio. Its holdings, quantities, buy-ins, and targets are deliberately invented. You can edit them; they last for this server session and reset when the app restarts. They are separate from My portfolio and are not a starting copy of your own holdings.

Explore demo uses public quotes, history, analytics and issuer ETF downloads. Initial quantities are sized once from available quotes and FX; subsequent refreshes preserve quantities and edits. The first load shows Preparing your demo… while prices arrive, then opens the overview automatically. If initialization cannot obtain prices, use Refresh prices or choose ? → Take the tour for the offline example. Missing fund downloads leave that fund whole.

docs.title: Take the tour
docs.text:
Choose Take the tour at the optional welcome prompt, or ? → Take the tour anytime. Not now dismisses the prompt. The app remembers dismissal for this computer's user account.

The tour uses invented prices, history and ETF weights without market requests. It opens its own fresh synthetic demo, even if you started from an empty or personal portfolio. Use Back, Next, or the chapter shortcuts. Try the highlighted chart when invited. Risk and a €500 contribution example are calculated for you. Finish, Skip tour, or Escape returns to your original workspace and view, including filters, without changing saved holdings or targets, Monitoring rules, or alert acknowledgments.

The Monitoring chapter first shows a plain MSCI World / 200-session SMA chart. It then configures an invented example; Next saves it only in the temporary tour workspace. Review its triggered condition, then try Acknowledge alert. The +10% threshold is chosen to demonstrate a trigger on synthetic history; it is not a suggested investment rule. Tour rules disappear when you leave. You can then repeat these actions yourself:

docs.title: 1. Understand Overview
docs.text:
1. Open Overview → Allocation. The offline demo starts at about €93,184, with deliberately uneven current weights against its saved targets.
  2. Select Equities in Category, or click that chart segment. The chart, table and value cards now describe that category. Its World and Emerging Markets position targets are 70% and 30% of Equities. Click the chart center or select Portfolio to return to the whole portfolio.
  3. Choose Performance. Compare Return (%) with Gain. These figures use recorded costs of currently held positions and exclude dividends and realized gains. Missing costs leave gaps rather than zero returns.
  4. Choose Analytics, then Calculate risk. The default uses three years against a global equity ETF benchmark. Read coverage and exclusions beside the result. It models today's allocation held constant, not your personal historical return. Offline history is invented.

The demo's top-level targets are Equities 60%, Money market 25%, Gold 10% and Crypto 5%. Live quotes move current weights, so do not expect live mode to match the offline figures exactly. See categories, performance and risk for details.

docs.title: 2. Look inside funds in Exposure
docs.text:
1. Open Exposure → Assets. Break down ETFs starts enabled. Turn it off to see whole securities, then on to see supported fund constituents combined with matching direct holdings. Your owned quantities do not change.
  2. Open an asset to inspect its contributing positions. Other retains the uncovered fund weight; it is not another position you own directly.
  3. Choose Themes & sectors. Money market, gold and crypto appear under No business sector; Unclassified retains genuinely missing sector data. The demo opens on Sector because it has no curated theme labels. Then choose Geography to explore regions and countries. Unknown geography stays explicit; overnight-rate exposure appears separately as Money market.
  4. Use Data & settings → ETF refresh & snapshots to check source dates and coverage. Individual ETFs controls which available funds expand.

Offline World and Emerging Markets snapshots contain invented company weights and small Other remainders of 1–1.5%. Live coverage depends on issuer downloads. Bond summaries and overnight-rate substitute baskets have separate meanings; read Exposure and ETFs before interpreting them.

docs.title: 3. Inspect positions
docs.text:
Open Positions and select a row for details and available price history. Use its pencil to edit, or Add position to try a new holding. A demo edit changes only the temporary demo. Position tools also offers Bulk add purchases, Update balances, Connect live prices and Import. Import opens transactions and works with existing holdings. Its Holdings snapshot option initializes an empty portfolio from a current holdings report.

A price chart is instrument history, not your return history. Update balances replaces current quantities; Bulk add purchases adds purchases or calculates the cost of shares already held. These are different actions. See Positions and buy-ins.

docs.title: 4. Try targets and a contribution plan
docs.text:
1. Open Rebalance → Targets. Inspect category targets relative to their parent and position targets relative to their own category. Complete sibling targets must total 100%; blank means unknown.
  2. Return to Plan. Keep Portfolio contribution, enter 500 in Contribution, then choose Calculate plan. Amounts use the portfolio currency. The demo already has the targets needed for this exercise.
  3. Read Suggested trades, Portfolio impact, and Plan details. The plan proposes purchases; it neither places orders nor saves new holdings. Purchase restrictions can leave money unallocated.
  4. To explore the three rebalancing modes, choose Within a category, then a Planning category. This reveals Rebalancing mode. Portfolio contribution has its own options and does not offer that mode selector.

For your own portfolio, missing targets or valuations can block a plan. Rebalance explains tolerances, minimum purchases and caps.

docs.title: Switch out of the demo
docs.text:
Finish or skip the tour first. In the header's Portfolio workspace dropdown, select My portfolio. Demo holdings are not copied. An empty workspace offers Start my portfolio; an existing workspace loads its saved holdings.

Open Portfolio settings → App & workspace to confirm the actual folder before saving. The installed app manages its persistent workspace for you. Use the same shortcut on subsequent starts; Storage explains default folders and remembered restored-workspace selections.

docs.title: Choose currency and optional categories
docs.text:
Choose Start my portfolio. In Set up your portfolio, select EUR, USD or GBP as the reporting currency; EUR is the default. Add categories one row at a time with optional targets. Enter adds the row and focuses the next empty name. Complete targets totaling 100% open All set?; review the table and choose Continue to first position. Unfinished targets can instead be saved with Save categories & continue and completed later.

Skip setup saves the selected currency without creating categories and opens Overview after the optional tour prompt. Choose Positions to add or import. If you save categories, the first-position form opens; Finish later leaves the categories saved without creating a holding. After saving or finishing that form, you return to Overview and the optional tour prompt.

docs.title: Save a first holding, or import
docs.text:
For manual entry, choose Positions → Add position. Search and select the correct listing, checking its exchange and currency, or choose Enter manually. Enter the quantity you currently hold. Buy-in cost and allocation targets are optional. Save position writes to My portfolio; check the saved row and its valuation status. A blank price is unknown, not zero. For an asset without a quote, provide a dated manual price under More details. For physical gold, choose Physical asset → Gold spot price and enter fine-gold weight; see physical gold.

For a holdings report, keep the portfolio empty and choose Import → Holdings snapshot, or the empty-list Import holdings button. Upload, map and review the report before Import reviewed positions. Check number formats, units and dates; saving cannot be undone by canceling the review afterwards. FinanzManager recognition is provisional. See Import for supported files and later live-price linking.

Next, check prices and cost coverage, then assign positions and complete targets in Rebalance → Targets. Category changes and position targets have separate saves. Missing buy-ins do not prevent allocation analysis. Change reporting currency later through Portfolio settings → Portfolio currency → Review currency change; inspect conversion gaps before applying. New buy-ins default to the reporting currency; original saved costs keep theirs.

docs.title: Make a backup and verify persistence
docs.text:
1. With My portfolio selected, save or cancel open edits. Open Portfolio settings → Create backup and wait for archive verification.
  2. Choose Download backup and save the .portfolio-backup.zip file to a protected backup location. It contains saved workspace files, including costs, currency, targets and ETF snapshots. Unsaved forms are not included. Demo and tour workspaces cannot be backed up through this action.
  3. Stop the app using Portfolio settings → App & workspace → Stop application or close its standalone Windows window. Closing a browser tab alone does not stop the server. Relaunch the same shortcut or data path and check your saved holding and reporting currency.

Keep backups private: they are unencrypted. Storage and recovery explains verified restore into a new folder, review/cancel behavior and switching workspaces. A backup should exist before you change files outside the app.

Use ? → User guide for version-matched help. Portfolio settings holds portfolio and workspace controls; the top-right app menu offers Light, Dark and System appearance. Hover or keyboard-focus help controls for units and scope.

docs.title: Import holdings and transactions
docs.text: Frozen candidate documentation · app 0.2.0 · source b810ada068f870d1319373d5258f456777f389f6

docs.title: Import holdings and transactions
docs.text:
Positions → Import opens transaction import. Transactions can be imported into an existing or empty portfolio; review their mappings and reconstructed balances before applying. See Import transactions.

Choose Holdings snapshot to initialize an empty portfolio from a current holdings report. For replacement balances in existing positions, use Update balances. Neither import performs ongoing synchronization.

docs.title: Export and review
docs.text:
FinanzManager-compatible column recognition is provisional: no specific tester export/version has been verified. Look for a current depot/holdings report and Bericht exportieren. Available formats and columns depend on your version. Use CSV, delimited TXT/TSV or Excel XLS/XLSX. QIF and PDF are unsupported.

  1. In Positions, choose Import → Holdings snapshot (or the empty-list Import holdings button) and upload one or more files, for example separate depot reports.
  2. Check worksheet, header row, delimiter, encoding and German/English number formatting. Inspect the preview before trusting suggested mappings.
  3. Map instrument name and quantity. When both Bank and FinanzManager quantities exist, explicitly select the intended source. Exclude headings and totals.
  4. Confirm quantities are shares/units and prices are amounts per unit. Convert nominal bond amounts and percentage quotes before import; the app does not infer that conversion.
  5. Optionally map identifiers, account, costs and dated snapshot prices. Review warnings and resolve duplicate positions. Names alone never merge instruments.
  6. Choose Import reviewed positions to save accepted fields. Use allocation setup afterwards; targets and classifications are not inferred from the report.

Costs may be average per unit or total cost of the remaining holding, with an acquisition currency. Leave unknown values blank. A WKN is not a quote ticker. An export price needs its date, currency and unit convention. It remains a manual snapshot, not an automatically refreshing price. Foreign snapshot prices use available FX, not historical FX on the export date; missing FX leaves value unknown.

Uploads and drafts remain in session memory through tab navigation. Cancel, completion or workspace switching clears them. Cancel writes no holdings. Accepted fields are saved locally with revision checking and private backups.

docs.title: Connect a live listing later
docs.text:
Open Positions → Connect live prices, select the imported instrument, search for a listing, and verify the ISIN and exchange. Existing ISINs must match. Missing results do not invalidate the saved position. WKN-only or ISIN-only holdings can remain unpriced until a suitable listing is available.

Linking can retain the dated manual price. Explicitly choose the switch to live pricing to clear manual prices across all account positions for that instrument. Quantity, buy-in, identity and allocation assignments stay saved. A connected ticker is not a guarantee that quotes will be available.

ETF discovery can separately use issuer-confirmed identity to install a breakdown; import review itself stays offline.

docs.title: Transaction CSV
docs.text:
Choose Positions → Import; Transactions is selected by default. Upload a CSV, map its assets to existing holdings or new positions, then review the transactions and forward-reconstructed balances. New positions are created only when you apply. An optional price listing connects normal current and historical market data. Existing holdings are matched by identifier, name, ISIN or ticker; crypto symbols also match ticker pairs such as BTC-EUR. Ambiguous matches require a choice. New assets receive exact listing suggestions, preferring the reporting currency. Crypto listings are checked for that currency in mixed portfolios too; other quote currencies remain available when no matching pair is found. Click the price-listing field to open its searchable popup. Suggestions appear immediately, with the reporting currency first; type a name, ticker or ISIN to search in the same popup. Each result shows its ticker, currency and exchange. Choosing a result updates the field and closes the popup. Escape or clicking outside keeps the previous selection. Suggestions, names and types remain editable; listing changes are saved together with applied transactions. The listing label identifies the quote pair; its quote currency is not added to the holding name. The Holding dropdown contains existing holdings and New position. Selecting New position splits that cell into the dropdown and an editable holding name beside it. The holding dropdown selects the destination; the price-listing popup selects the market-data source. Edited names survive listing changes and navigation. Automatically suggested types can be reviewed under Asset types & categories. Each new holding has a separate Category choice, initially Unassigned, using the portfolio's leaf categories. This also assigns fully sold holdings and their retained history. Type and price listing never choose a category automatically. Existing holdings keep their categories and targets; new position targets remain undecided. Category choices survive Back to import. If categories or targets change during review, reload and review again; an unavailable category must be changed explicitly before application. Create categories in Rebalance → Targets when needed. Show transactions for filters the review table by asset, including received exchange legs and asset fees. It does not exclude transactions from the import.

Before upload, there is no review to cancel. After upload, Discard review clears the file and unsaved choices and returns to the uploader. Changing tabs retains the draft. Saved transactions are not deleted by discarding their review.

The template has seven columns:

Column Meaning reference Stable unique reference across your transaction files; retain it when correcting a row. date Transaction date, YYYY-MM-DD. type buy, sell, income, fee, exchange, transfer_in, transfer_out, or opening. asset The asset to map to a holding. quantity Positive units; zero for cash income/fees. amount Trade consideration excluding fees, income value, external transfer value, or starting acquisition cost. Blank means unknown. currency Currency of the amount.

Optional columns are fee, fee_currency, fee_asset, received_asset, received_quantity, acquisition_cost, acquisition_currency, order, estimated and note. Exchange rows need the received asset and quantity. In-kind income adds units; cash income has zero quantity. A fee with positive quantity is paid in that asset; a cash fee has zero quantity and a monetary amount. For a transfer in, amount is its boundary valuation and acquisition_cost is its carried basis. These values need not match. opening is a starting balance, not a purchase or contribution. Split and tax events are also supported.

Omitting the optional fee column declares no additional fees. If included, blank fees remain unknown; enter zero when none were paid. estimated=yes marks supplied amounts as estimates. Do not use zero to represent an unknown value. File order is the initial order for same-day transactions; supply order when a different execution order is known. Dates are not converted into invented execution times. When dependent transactions on one day come from separate files or incompatible clocks, Review same-day order shows the affected entries before balance review. Enter distinct order numbers, earlier first, and choose Use reviewed order. Original timestamps remain retained; PDF statement times without a timezone are never treated as UTC. Already applied history keeps its accepted order until an explicit review changes it.

Use Save evidence only to retain the upload without changing active balances. Mapped transactions appear in the usual Transactions view. Saved imports for new positions can be reopened from the import screen. Review against portfolio opens the same reconciliation screen used for manual and PDF transaction history. Back to import retains the mapping and name edits. Reviewing writes nothing; the apply action saves the reviewed holdings and history together. For assets without a recorded starting balance, it previews zero holdings before the first movement and states that assumption beside the apply actions. Applying confirms that starting point. If the export begins after you already held assets, choose Import options → Before the first transaction → Earlier holdings and supply an opening balance in the CSV or the holding's History before applying. The ending reference is only a comparison; it never supplies a balancing opening.

The comparison shows whether units and acquisition costs match current holdings. The final apply action accepts the displayed reconstruction; a matching balance does not itself prove completeness because missing movements can cancel out. Similar transactions are shown once as a group, with all entries retained by default. Open the group to exclude pending entries; balances recompute from that selection. The final apply action accepts the selection, without separate pairwise acknowledgments. Excluded source evidence remains saved. The group shows whether all entries reconcile to an existing holding; a new holding's zero placeholder is never presented as an independently recorded ending balance. Different recorded execution times distinguish otherwise identical transactions. When either entry has only a date, matching economic details still appear in the similar-transactions group.

Apply history makes the reviewed ledger authoritative for the resulting holding. For multiple holdings, accept each displayed balance and choose Apply reviewed holdings. Each acceptance advances to the next unreviewed holding; reviewed holdings are marked in the selector. You can revisit them without accepting them again. Nothing is applied until every holding is reviewed and you choose the final apply action. There is no separate completeness declaration. Estimates stay labelled, and missing prices or amounts still limit their dependent metrics. Application replaces the managed balance; it does not add the same trades to the existing snapshot again.

After import, use the normal Transactions list to edit or remove entries, regardless of whether they came from CSV, PDF or manual entry. Exchanges, transfers and fees paid from another asset are reviewed with all affected holdings. Original evidence remains retained. Reimporting the same references does not duplicate transactions or undo later edits/removals. Moving rows within an export keeps their previously accepted order; use an explicit order to correct chronology. Changed source rows show their changed fields and require approval individually, including a warning when they replace a later edit or removal. Economically similar rows from different sources require a review rather than automatic deletion.

Prepare wallet/staking movements and personal approximations before import when one asset-level history is sufficient. Preserve fees and income once, and retain unknown facts as unknown. The application does not infer economic meaning from export labels. Older transaction formats, checkpoints and unresolved inventory records remain readable for compatibility. The separate asset-history diagnostic is retired; all results use normal history, daily TWR and annualized XIRR.

docs.title: Install and run
docs.text: Frozen candidate documentation · app 0.2.0 · source b810ada068f870d1319373d5258f456777f389f6

docs.title: Packaged application
docs.text:
Download a release from the repository's Releases page. Before the first official release, download a successful Build candidate Actions artifact while signed into GitHub. Extract that download once to find the installer and portable archive; candidates are test builds, not official releases. Verified local candidates may also be provided directly when Actions is unavailable. Use the installer supplied with that candidate's checksum and test record; a Windows Setup EXE does not need an additional ZIP wrapper.

Windows: run portfolio-breakdown-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe. Setup installs for your current user, creates a Start Menu entry, and optionally a desktop shortcut. Python and uv are not required. Keep the proposed application directory; your portfolio lives separately. Setup offers Microsoft's Evergreen WebView2 runtime if it is missing (internet is needed for that prerequisite). You can instead deselect WebView2 and use the installed Portfolio Breakdown (browser) shortcut. No automatic application updates are installed.

Open Portfolio Breakdown from the Start Menu. Its own window displays the intro while the app loads. F11 switches between maximized and borderless views; borderless mode also has an Exit button. Links to other sites open in your normal browser. Closing the app window stops its owned server. Launching again focuses the existing window for that workspace. The portable alternative is to extract the Windows application ZIP and run Portfolio Breakdown.exe; keep the complete extracted folder, including its _internal-<build> runtime directory. --browser selects the browser fallback.

Linux (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 x64): install the .deb with your package manager and launch Portfolio Breakdown Experimental from the applications menu. The package retains the name portfolio-breakdown-experimental. Check the release notes for that installer’s acceptance status and desktop limitations.

For browser mode, extract the application .tar.gz archive and run ./portfolio-app. Keep its whole folder together.

macOS (experimental): on Apple Silicon with macOS 15 or later, open the DMG and drag Portfolio Breakdown Experimental into Applications, then launch it there. Python is bundled; installing Python or uv is unnecessary. Intel Macs are not supported. This installer has ad-hoc integrity signing only, without a Developer ID signature or notarization. Gatekeeper rejects quarantined copies; interactive approval and real browser-download installation remain unverified. Automated packaged-app checks do not establish that first-install experience. Consult the release notes before downloading; experimental Mac builds may be omitted from a release if their automated checks fail.

Initial acceptance targets are Windows 11 and Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 x64. An unsigned candidate may trigger Windows reputation warnings; a successful build alone is not native acceptance. Verify that the file came from the intended candidate.

docs.title: Launch and stop
docs.text: Launch the installed app from its Start Menu entry or shortcut. To stop it, close the standalone window, or choose Portfolio settings → App & workspace → Stop application in browser mode. Closing a browser tab alone leaves the server running; relaunch the same shortcut to reopen it.

docs.title: Advanced launch options
docs.text:
For recovery or a custom workspace, open a terminal in the application install folder, not the portfolio data folder. On Windows, use PowerShell and the bundled console companion portfolio-app.exe (normally under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Portfolio Breakdown). These commands use the installed app and do not require Python or uv:

.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\workspace" --server.port=8502
.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\workspace" --stop

For the Linux browser archive, open a terminal in the extracted application folder:

./portfolio-app --data-dir /path/to/workspace --server.port=8502
./portfolio-app --data-dir /path/to/workspace --stop

For the installed Ubuntu .deb, use its launcher from any terminal:

portfolio-breakdown-experimental --data-dir /path/to/workspace
portfolio-breakdown-experimental --data-dir /path/to/workspace --stop

On Mac, use the console companion inside the app copied to Applications:

"/Applications/Portfolio Breakdown Experimental.app/Contents/MacOS/portfolio-cli" --data-dir /path/to/workspace
"/Applications/Portfolio Breakdown Experimental.app/Contents/MacOS/portfolio-cli" --data-dir /path/to/workspace --stop

Adjust the quoted app path if installed elsewhere. Both native launchers accept --browser for browser presentation. Mac command paths follow the bundle layout; personal-Mac installation and quarantine approval remain unverified.

Other advanced examples in this guide use the Windows console companion. Substitute the launcher for your installation above, using the same options and OS-appropriate paths. Recovery commands such as --stop, --backup-to and --restore-from do not open a native window. For a normal Windows window launch with custom options, use & ".\Portfolio Breakdown.exe" --data-dir "C:\path\to\workspace". Portable installs can create a shortcut with --install-shortcut; recreate it after moving the application folder.

Choose your own directory; the example paths are placeholders. The app binds to 127.0.0.1. By default it chooses another free port when 8501 is busy; an explicit occupied port fails. Repeated window launches focus the existing window; browser launches reopen the managed instance. Independent workspaces can use separate ports.

Use --stop with the same data directory if the interface is unavailable. Packaged browser launches normally run in the background. --foreground keeps a packaged launch attached for diagnostics; --no-browser suppresses automatic browser opening. Stop an existing instance before changing its command-line demo/live launch mode.

docs.title: Update or remove
docs.text:
Read the version 0.2.0 release and upgrade notes before updating an existing workspace, especially if you will apply transaction history or record futures/accounts.

  1. Stop the old app and back up the workspace.
  2. Run the new Windows Setup, install the new Ubuntu .deb with sudo apt install ./portfolio-breakdown-experimental_<version>_amd64.deb, or replace the Mac app in Applications with the copy from the new DMG. For portable archives, extract into a new application directory.
  3. Launch from the same shortcut or with the same custom data directory. Check holdings, targets, prices and the reported version before retiring the old application.
  4. Recreate shortcuts if its path changed. For rollback after a data-format change, restore the old backup into a new directory and use the matching app.

Do not overwrite an older backup. For an installed Windows app, use Settings → Apps → Portfolio Breakdown → Uninstall. For Ubuntu use sudo apt remove portfolio-breakdown-experimental. On Mac, move the stopped Portfolio Breakdown Experimental.app from Applications to Trash. For portable apps, remove the stopped app's directory and shortcut. These operations leave the separate portfolio workspace in place. Shared WebView2 is retained.

The app is GPL-3.0-only, without warranty under its license. Bundles include third-party notices; corresponding source and build material accompany releases.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
This is an alternative for contributors or people choosing to run a checkout. Skip this section if you installed the packaged app.

Install uv, obtain the repository at the intended source commit, and run these commands from its root. The package requires Python 3.12 or newer; uv manages the environment.

uv sync --locked
uv run portfolio-app --version
uv run portfolio-app

On Windows, uv run portfolio-desktop starts the standalone window directly from source; no executable rebuild is needed while iterating. Restart after Python changes. uv run portfolio-app retains the browser development workflow.

To open the guide locally from a source checkout, build it before launching:

uv sync --locked --group docs
uv run mkdocs build --strict
uv run portfolio-app

Without a local documentation build, source help links to the published development guide, which may be unavailable before Pages publication. Packaged candidates include their matching guide and need no documentation build. If packaged help reports that the bundled guide is unavailable, reinstall the complete app. The app will not silently open a different version's guide.

Use a locked checkout or frozen candidate to reproduce a tested environment. A uv tool install installation resolves its dependencies separately and does not consume the checkout's lockfile.

Source launches run attached to the terminal; Ctrl+C stops them. For an offline synthetic demo, run uv run portfolio-app --demo --offline-demo. To choose a separate workspace, append --data-dir /path/to/synthetic-workspace.

To update a source installation, back up and stop the app, update to the chosen commit and run uv sync --locked. A uv tool installation can be removed with uv tool uninstall portfolio-breakdown. Migrate and verify checkout-local data before deleting a checkout. See Source development for tests and preview instructions.

docs.title: Monitoring and alerts
docs.text: Frozen candidate documentation · app 0.2.0 · source b810ada068f870d1319373d5258f456777f389f6

docs.title: Monitoring and alerts
docs.text:
Monitoring explores indicators without adding an asset to your portfolio. On a fresh visit, Browse opens MSCI World in EUR with a 200-session SMA and an empty trigger threshold. This Untracked preview shows prices and SMA only, without rule bands or condition status, and does not enable alerts. Existing saved rules continue monitoring independently. Enter a threshold to preview its bands and condition; Track rule becomes available once the required inputs and market history are present. Clearing the threshold returns to the plain chart.

Under Browse, Market indices offers a fixed set of broad benchmarks: MSCI World, MSCI Emerging Markets and MSCI ACWI, each with published net-return levels in EUR, USD or GBP. Portfolio assets separately lists the unique tickers of currently held assets, excluding cash, derivatives and zero holdings. Provider ticker accepts an exact Yahoo Finance symbol for other instruments. Compare completed closes with an SMA and your trigger/approaching boundaries, then name the rule and choose Track rule in the save row above the chart. Tracked rules provides details, editing, pause/resume and deletion. Position details offer Track this asset; account and collateral views offer Create account alert.

For an offline introduction, choose ? → Take the tour and use the chapter shortcuts to reach Monitoring. Its trend, saved rule, triggered alert and acknowledgment use a fresh temporary synthetic workspace. Your existing rules and acknowledgments are preserved.

docs.title: Moving-average rules
docs.text:
The 200-session preset uses 200 completed trading observations, not 200 calendar days. The 10-month preset uses ten consecutive completed month-end closes, not all daily observations during ten months. Missing months are not filled. A newly completed close enters the average. Months finalize when the next local calendar month begins; a provider bar still developing during the trading session does not count as a completed close.

Rules compare 100 × (price / SMA − 1) with an inclusive threshold. For example, a below rule with a −2% trigger fires at or below 98% of its SMA. A one-percentage- point approaching band begins at −1%. Above rules reverse the comparison.

Choose completed daily close, completed month-end close, or a timestamped intraday observation. Intraday mode normally uses the last completed SMA. Include developing period, under Timing & data freshness, instead combines the current observation with the preceding N−1 completed periods. This changes the reference during the period and is explicitly labeled.

Closing-price history is the default for stocks and ETFs. Dividend-adjusted history is a separate selection, rebased to current quote units for comparison. Provider split adjustments remain part of the chosen history. An index retains its named currency and price/net/gross-return convention. Rules retain their native series currency when the portfolio reporting currency changes.

Direct MSCI references provide daily net-return levels, not intraday quotes. Choose an alternative instrument explicitly if you want intraday tracking; the app never silently substitutes an ETF. Regular-session provider quotes may be delayed. Freshness limits are editable: defaults are 30 minutes for intraday rules and seven days for close/account rules, entered in minutes, hours or days. Intraday rules can therefore show stale outside trading hours. Missing metadata, insufficient history, stale inputs or failed requests withhold a new signal and any all-clear.

Yahoo can include entirely empty rows in historical downloads. Rows without any OHLC prices or trading volume are omitted, without filling prices; the SMA uses available closing observations. Partial bars with a missing close, or missing adjusted prices, remain data errors. Data details shows omitted-row counts, the source, its available history and retrieval time.

docs.title: Historical browsing
docs.text:
Chart period offers one, three, five or ten years, all available history, dotcom and GFC periods, or custom start and end dates. Indicators are calculated using the full history before the chart is cropped, preserving their warm-up. Historical-period metrics describe the final close in that period and, when a threshold is configured, are labeled Historical condition. With a blank threshold, no condition is shown. Browsing the past neither creates alerts nor changes a saved rule's live evaluation period; it is not a strategy backtest.

The MSCI source is requested from 2000 onward; actual availability varies by index. An ETF or other instrument cannot show prices from before its own available history. Missing initial SMA values are left blank until sufficient earlier observations exist. The app never silently substitutes an older proxy instrument.

docs.title: Account rules
docs.text:
LTV divides recorded account loans plus negative cash obligations by the current gross value of your explicitly selected backing securities and positive cash balances. Cash uses the canonical account balance, so adopted cash is not counted twice. Linked securities remain ordinary holdings. No haircuts apply to this gross LTV measure. Pending transfers and futures notional are excluded. Choose your own maximum and warning LTV ratios; the app does not infer a broker's liquidation threshold.

Maintenance headroom uses the existing pledged collateral after haircuts and entered maintenance requirements. Its percentage is 100 × (eligible collateral − maintenance requirement) / maintenance requirement. Choose trigger and warning headroom thresholds. The details show monetary headroom and the date/source of the entered requirement.

Rules fix their calculation currency and show included inputs. Missing valuation or FX withholds the result. Positive debt with zero backing triggers an explicit undefined-ratio alert; zero debt with zero backing and zero maintenance requirements make their respective percentage metrics inapplicable. These are user-defined limits and declared coverage, not broker-specific liquidation models.

docs.title: Delivery and history
docs.text:
Monitoring runs while an app session is open, checking every five minutes with a one-minute heartbeat. Last rule check and Check all rules now appear only in Tracked rules and refer to all enabled saved rules. A completed pass can include stale or unavailable results; check each rule's Data column. Refresh market data in Browse refreshes the selected instrument's prices and history without checking saved rules. Closing the app, suspending the computer or losing the session interrupts monitoring. This release does not install an operating-system background service or send external messages.

Approaching conditions show a banner inside Monitoring by default. Triggered conditions also open an acknowledgment dialog on any tab, including Browse and inline editors. An already open modal defers the alert until it closes. A rule can instead use banners only or the notification center only. Notifications explain the affected rule and offer View rule. Existing data-quality notices have specific review actions.

Reading and acknowledging are separate. Opening Notifications marks entries read; Acknowledge alert in the pop-up or Acknowledge in Notifications silences that alert and hides its banner. The current condition remains visible in Tracked rules. Full recovery to normal rearms the rule. Escalation from approaching to triggered produces a new alert, but unchanged checks and threshold jitter within one warning episode do not repeat pop-ups. Data failures preserve the last valid condition with an explicit stale label rather than treating missing data as normal.

History retains observations and alert episodes from creation onward. Available missed completed-close events can be recovered on reopening and are labeled with the original observation date and later recording time. Intraday and account history is never reconstructed across offline gaps. Charts show source history; recorded observations show what monitoring actually evaluated. Provider revisions can change a historical chart without rewriting the observation log.

Editing or pausing/resuming creates a new rule revision and evaluation baseline. Deleting a rule preserves its recorded history. Data lives in private monitoring.json and is included in workspace backups. Rule edits retain document backups; frequent observation writes use atomic replacement without making a full backup copy each time. Market downloads stay in private caches.

docs.title: Prices and performance
docs.text: Frozen candidate documentation · app 0.2.0 · source b810ada068f870d1319373d5258f456777f389f6

docs.title: Valuation and freshness
docs.text:
Reporting value = quantity × quote price × reporting currency per unit of quote currency

Provider prices use the latest available unadjusted daily close; the current bar can still change. They are not guaranteed real-time execution quotes. Quote currency comes from provider metadata, not ticker suffixes. Recognized pence/cents units are converted to major currency before FX. A saved manual price overrides provider pricing until cleared. Buy-in is never substituted for market price.

Missing ticker, currency, FX or quote leaves a position unvalued, not worth zero. A zero-quantity position has zero current value without requiring a quote. View price details for separate quote/FX timestamps, ages and reasons.

Quotes and FX refresh in the background using private caches. Normal attempts are limited to once per 15 minutes per key, including failures. Refresh prices bypasses that interval. Failed refreshes can retain the last successful quote as cached fallback. Old data is not newly observed data; inspect dates across market closures. Crypto quotes older than 24 hours have a continuous-market note.

docs.title: Gains and returns
docs.text:
Choose EUR, USD or GBP during manual setup or in Portfolio settings → Portfolio currency. Existing portfolios default to EUR. Changing this setting recalculates values and gains from original records; it does not change purchase amounts or currencies. Review affected positions before applying. Monetary planning inputs and previous plans are cleared when currency changes.

Allocation and Performance All share total known gain: recorded realized and unrealized gains plus recorded distributions and interest, less recorded costs once. They use the same current valuation inputs, currency and scope, including retained closed positions. Quote and FX timestamps remain visible in price details; current inputs do not fill missing historical observations. Category comparison uses the same monetary calculation. ETF look-through does not redefine costs.

The Overview percentage is cumulative time-weighted return (TWR) over the supported recorded interval. It neutralizes external contributions and withdrawals using daily valuations and the daily cash-flow convention described below. It is not gain divided by remaining cost or net capital. Annualized return is separately money-weighted (XIRR), reflecting contribution amounts and timing. Neither percentage is inferred from a partial monetary subtotal. Position details retain separately labelled unrealized gain and cost-based return.

Partial means supported known components are shown, with missing facts in metric help. Summary-only holdings contribute their known unrealized gain; snapshot histories carry known opening unrealized gain but cannot establish earlier realized gains or income. Unreviewed records can support a recorded subtotal, never complete returns. Unknown amounts, unsupported actions and missing FX are not zero.

Cash balances without a recorded cost/conversion basis show N/A — cash balance for purchase-based performance. They remain in portfolio value and allocation, but do not produce missing-buy-in warnings or reduce coverage of eligible positions. Balance increases from deposits or futures settlements are not inferred as cash investment gains. Interest is separate. Foreign cash still changes reporting value with current FX; calculating its FX gain needs a recorded opening or conversion basis. Explicit cash costs, including incomplete conversions, retain the existing cost-based calculation and coverage checks.

Each purchase, including fees, is converted separately. A supplied converted cost takes precedence over a supplied rate, which takes precedence over historical market FX. Historical lookup uses the purchase date or the most recent available observation within the preceding seven days. It never uses a future observation. Market rates can differ from actual broker settlement rates. Same-currency costs need no purchase date or conversion.

A position with incomplete costs has no complete cost-based gain, while its available current value still counts toward portfolio value and allocation. Transaction CSV can retain supplied acquisition-cost and monetary-valuation estimates, with their sources. Affected gains show an approximate status. Applying transaction history does not certify estimated amounts as exact; the label remains while the calculation depends on those estimates. Costed units can contribute a partial unrealized gain while other units retain unknown cost; the unknown units are never treated as free. Independently supported recorded income or realized gains can still contribute to an explicitly partial monetary subtotal. Complete, Partial and Unavailable describe coverage. A partial return is not the return of the entire category. Zero cost permits an absolute gain but no cost-based percentage. TWR/XIRR have their own flow and valuation requirements.

For old costs without dates, supply a converted total or exchange rate, or explicitly confirm a latest FX estimate. Portfolio settings lets you select affected positions and review their rates before confirming. Estimates may hide currency gains or losses, remain labelled, and keep their confirmed rates across refreshes and restarts. An undated conversion or estimate applies only to its saved target currency; switching again may create new coverage gaps.

Separately labelled ordinary-holding unrealized figures exclude dividends and realized gains. Purchase fees affect results only when included in recorded cost. Reconcile remaining-position costs after sales or corporate actions. Expanded ETF constituents have unavailable performance: current weights cannot reconstruct their historical costs. Whole-fund performance remains usable in instruments mode. Labels follow the same path splits as allocation.

Futures investment details retain a separate recorded-performance basis: cumulative net P&L across open and closed contracts, including fees and manually entered taxes, divided by fixed initial allocated capital. Settlement does not erase gains. Allocation changes affect capital value, not profit. Current reporting FX converts native amounts; historical FX performance of contributed capital is not inferred. See Investment capital and contract history.

docs.title: Market-price history
docs.text:
In position details, History → Price provides 1M, 6M, 1Y, 5Y and Max views of closing prices in the portfolio reporting currency, without dividend reinvestment. When the instrument's quote currency differs, the currency selector beside the period offers both currency codes (for example, EUR and USD). This is instrument history, not personal return history. It does not know your purchase dates or cash flows.

History loads in the background and caches for one hour. A failed request waits 60 seconds before an automatic retry; Retry history bypasses the wait. Manual/unsupported instruments can have no chart. Normal demo mode uses public history; explicit offline demo history is invented. The separate risk calculation uses adjusted prices and historical FX.

docs.title: Personal history
docs.text:
CSV, PDF and manually entered transactions use the same history and controls. Source details are available with each transaction; they do not change its calculations or editability. Exchanges and transfers are single economic events whose connected holdings are reviewed together.

Explicitly supplied estimates can support daily TWR and annualized XIRR. Affected results retain the estimate qualification in gain/TWR and annualized-return tooltips, without separate estimate captions. Missing transaction details and market observations remain separate limitations. An estimated acquisition cost does not by itself make a return estimated when that return uses independently known cash flows and market values. Unknown amounts stay unknown; a matching ending quantity does not certify complete history. The former separate daily-Dietz diagnostic is retired. Existing diagnostic settings are preserved but no longer affect the application.

The History → Holdings position view and Overview → Performance show personal history separately from market-price charts and current unrealized gains. History is optional; charts stay hidden until at least two supported values exist. Positions open on History, with Holdings selected when useful transaction history exists and Price otherwise. Positions without recorded history evidence show the price chart directly, without the selector. The Holdings / Price selector remembers your explicit choice for each position during the session. Without applied history, Holdings offers a route to add and review transactions. The other position tabs stay in the same order. Overview remembers your selected view for each portfolio, including after a browser refresh or app restart. With no saved choice it opens Performance when useful history exists, otherwise Allocation. Allocation's percentage gain uses full-history TWR; when unavailable, its tooltip explains the missing evidence. Position details share one row above the chart selector: Position value with personal gain, Invested capital, and Annualized return. Switching chart type, range or hover does not change these headlines. Dated figures stay in the chart tooltip. Details contains return on cost and unrealized gain. Without applied history, capital is the recorded acquisition cost, gain is unrealized only, and annualized return is unavailable. Overview keeps its own history summary above the chart. The category comparison stays visible below history, without repeating the category or position tables. Choosing another view retains its usual current-portfolio summary. Use 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y or All to look back from today. The chart axis ends today; period gain uses the first and latest supported valuations in the selected window. Annualized return uses the full recorded interval. Verified closed-market endpoints can use the last eligible closing quote, retaining its actual as-of date. Stuttgart listings are recognized from the provider's exchange and timezone metadata and use the Stuttgart calendar, including its published trading holidays. A metadata refresh updates previously downloaded evidence without inventing weekend quotes. A missing price on a scheduled trading day still blocks the affected valuation. The latest valuation date remains visible. Lines connect neighboring known values across missing observations; this does not supply prices for calculation purposes.

History follows the main Category selector: Portfolio includes the full portfolio; a category includes its current source-position membership, including retained closed positions. This does not reconstruct past category assignments. Removed closed positions with no current assignment remain in Unassigned and the portfolio total, including the category comparison. Accounts include cash, debt, pending claims and actual futures. An account whose components span categories needs dated allocations before category history can be shown; it is never silently counted in full or omitted. Allocated futures strategy capital is also unavailable at category level without that support. Unadopted legacy liabilities and simulations cannot silently disappear from a whole-portfolio result.

All means total known gain, not necessarily the full ownership period. Missing opening prices never silently substitute a shorter interval. Complete histories start empty before the first purchase, include that payment and fees, and retain gains after liquidation. A confirmed empty start needs no positive snapshot.

The solid Value line is the selected holding or portfolio's market value. The thinner dashed Invested capital line starts with known opening acquisition cost for securities, and recorded opening equity for accounts, then adds external contributions less withdrawals. Value minus capital equals cumulative known gain at the same date. After disposals this is not remaining acquisition cost and can be zero or negative. Unsupported capital remains unavailable. Changing the chart period preserves the basis. Nothing before an opening snapshot is represented as zero value or gain.

For example, an invented snapshot with cost 8,000 and market value 10,000 starts with capital 8,000 and known gain 2,000. Later value 11,000 means known gain 3,000, but post-snapshot return is 10% before annualization. The earlier gain has unknown timing and does not enter returns. Backfill replaces this bridge rather than adding reconstructed gains to it a second time. If cost is unknown, measured post-snapshot gain may be shown as partial while capital stays unavailable. Move anywhere across the plot to inspect a date and formatted values together. The vertical guide snaps to observations; it does not invent interpolated prices. If series have different observation dates, the tooltip shows each differing date beside its value. The value and invested capital boxes follow the hovered observations and show their dates. Click the gain badge to toggle between an amount and cumulative TWR. The metric name and period appear only in a concise tooltip. Gain beside the value shows the selected-period gain at rest and cumulative recorded gain to the hovered date during inspection. Ranges covering the entire holding period use total known gain, just like All. Leaving the chart restores the latest value and selected-period gain. Annualized return stays fixed across both period selection and hover; its tooltip gives the calculation dates. Missing opening data or incomplete full-history coverage withholds this return rather than substituting a shorter interval. A quiet note below the chart indicates missing valuations; no values are interpolated for the boxes or returns. A missing daily value need not prevent endpoint-based returns. Returns for both All and a selected period remain unavailable if a later recorded event lacks an ending valuation. The timeline includes linked-security cash movements, incoming transfers and separately dated fees. Those fee dates also count when checking for known negative equity, even if the balance later recovers.

Correct market data provides focused forms for missing or incorrect dated prices and exchange rates. Known dates, holdings and currencies are preselected; only the selected holdings' observations are shown. Advanced corrections retains whole-selection valuations, exact cash-flow boundary values and cash adjustment classification. Available prices and FX load automatically; Retry prices is shown after an unsuccessful refresh. Downloads include accepted exact-contract settlement marks. It does not create trades, distributions or splits. Downloaded closes are converted back to the units traded on each date using the provider's split evidence, without dividend reinvestment or automatic price repair. Manual observations take precedence. For prices, optional Quote provenance contains Source, Quote listing, Exchange calendar and Exchange timezone. Corrections initially retain the saved quote's details; missing dates can receive explicitly supplied details. These entries are your evidence, not automatic verification. The historical quote listing does not change the holding's current listing. Saving preserves the original observation and records a manual correction, so later downloads do not overwrite it. Saved market data shows actual source and listing/calendar/timezone details; manual source descriptions are marked manual:.

Prices must cover required valuation boundaries; only verified closed sessions can use the preceding eligible close. Exact-contract futures marks use the supported Eurex session calendar too, so weekend funding can use the preceding session's settlement without inventing a weekend mark. Missing trading-day marks and unsupported calendars remain gaps. For Saturday/Sunday valuations, an absent closing FX rate uses the immediately preceding Friday's closing rate, or the prior scheduled close when Friday itself is a documented FX holiday. Thus a Monday contribution can use Friday's supported closing price and FX for its opening valuation, without inventing Sunday observations. The same rule covers explicitly documented FX closing-session holidays for EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, JPY, CAD, AUD and NZD pairs, including New Year's Day 2025. The historical date list uses OANDA's holiday schedule and LEAN's Forex-oanda calendar. Evening holiday reopenings start the next closing session. Other bank/equity holidays and undocumented future holidays do not establish an FX closure; maintainers must verify additional dates before adding them. Actual dated closing FX takes precedence. Missing scheduled closes are not filled from older or later rates. Quote and FX as-of dates remain visible. Transaction payments, fees and acquisition-cost conversions still require their own dated conversion evidence. Gaps are not interpolated or filled with current quotes. Missing data can be entered manually. Corrections retain original observations.

Applied history is the authoritative ledger for the resulting holdings and accounts. Apply history accepts the balances shown in reconciliation; there is no separate completeness confirmation. Gains and returns remain available as new prices arrive, provided their required inputs are supported. A newer valuation date does not invalidate the applied ledger.

Replacement balances interrupt an interval, and unresolved cash adjustments must be classified as external flows, income or expenses, or retained as boundaries. An edit to remaining acquisition cost alone does not interrupt period gain, TWR or XIRR: those use market values and cash flows. It does prevent carrying the old cost basis through the edit as complete lifetime capital or gain; independently supported gain components remain available. Unknown amounts, missing market data and unsupported earlier periods remain explicit limitations. Applying records does not prove that unrecorded real-world activity never occurred; calculations describe the records supplied. After a dated replacement opening, later periods can use that opening even if an older checkpoint lacked an observation date. Returns across the replacement remain unsupported.

Account cash openings precede separately recorded same-day account trades, fees and external funding; these events must not disappear into the first closing valuation. Security starting balances remain end-of-day snapshots, and derived security payments already included in an account opening are not posted again. An explicitly newly funded account instead starts at zero before its first-day transactions, including linked securities purchases and fees. A confirmed empty security opening dated the preceding day is consistent with that declaration. If an internal transfer or asset-paid fee on the selected start date crosses a new account's opening boundary and an existing account or holding's closing snapshot, period gain and returns remain unavailable. Choose a start date before or after that day; the supported ending value remains available. Same-day flow order must be explicit for exact TWR.

Metric Required evidence Historical value Dated holdings, cash, debt, claims, prices and FX, or an explicitly supplied total valuation Invested capital Known opening cost/account equity plus supported classified net external flows Total known gain Ending value minus capital, including known opening gains; partial components stay labelled Period gain Ending value minus opening market value minus net external contributions Annualized money-weighted return Endpoint values and complete dated external flows with a numerically verified unique XIRR Time-weighted return Supported daily flow boundaries and complete dated external flows; exact event valuations when explicitly requesting the exact method

Purchases paid from included cash, transfers between included accounts, borrowing with its matching debt, and futures settlement are internal movements. Crossing the selected scope changes that treatment. Dividends and interest are income; withdrawals are separate flows. Fees reduce results once. Remaining acquisition cost and cumulative purchases are not net contributions. Futures notional and allocated principal are not extra wealth; settled profit already resides in cash.

Money-weighted returns use actual elapsed days divided by 365 and can work without daily valuations. The annualized-return tooltip identifies short recorded intervals. Same-day periods, known negative-equity intervals and unverified solutions have no annualized return. Negative equity is checked at recorded event-day closes and valuation dates, including values reconstructed from prices, FX, cash and debt. Negative cash covered by other assets, and a negative invested-capital line after withdrawals, do not themselves make portfolio equity negative. Missing valuations remain unknown; intraday losses without recorded valuation evidence are not inferred. Empty inception and terminal liquidation are supported when dated flows establish a unique result. TWR can link explicitly valued funded intervals separated by an empty period; money appearing without funding is invalid. Mixed-sign cash flows are eligible only when the solver establishes a unique, numerically verified XIRR. Multiple roots, no solution and uncertain numerical conditioning are different from missing transactions. Supported long schedules use a verified uniqueness certificate. An XIRR calculation limit means the bounded solver could not verify the full schedule within its work limit; unusually complex schedules can still remain unavailable. The app never shortens the period, guesses a root or substitutes return on cost. Conventional schedules retain a separate fast path.

Ordinary TWR uses a daily convention: incoming capital is available at the start of the day and outgoing capital leaves at its end. Chain daily factors (ending equity + withdrawals) / (beginning equity + contributions) and subtract one. This convention does not reconstruct intraday prices. Flow-free intervals can telescope without inventing intermediate observations; required flow boundaries must still be supported. Negative equity remains unsupported.

Same-date charges belong to their economic transaction: purchase fees increase contributions, while sale/distribution charges reduce proceeds. Separately dated charges keep their dates. Recorded fees and taxes reduce returns once. Included cash and securities trade internally; external fee funding enters once. Scope membership determines which payments cross the boundary. Embedded fund expenses are already in market prices and are not deducted again.

Exact event TWR remains an explicit calculation option. It requires genuine ordering and supported before/after event valuations, and includes the event's fees and income. Execution prices may support standalone security boundaries, but do not value other assets in a portfolio. Neither method changes saved trade dates. Historical value points and monetary gains can remain useful when returns cannot be calculated. The affected metric’s help explains its own missing requirements; other metrics do not inherit that restriction.

Original acquisition costs remain separate from opening market value, so gains before the tracking boundary are not attributed to the tracked period. FIFO is analytical cost accounting, not a tax report. Complex unsupported corporate actions must remain unresolved until sufficient records or a new opening boundary exist.

Position Details separates recorded realized gain, net income, other expenses, purchase payments and net sale proceeds. Remaining acquisition cost belongs to the unsold FIFO lots; cumulative purchase payments include all recorded purchases and their charges. Sale proceeds include returned principal, whereas realized gain deducts the sold lots' costs. Buy fees enter lot cost, sell and distribution charges reduce their proceeds, and other expenses are deducted separately. These components reconcile to total gain for an ordinary complete trade history. Transfers preserve lot costs but cross performance scopes at market value, so their acquisition-cost breakdown and scope gain have different boundaries.

Imported swaps and rewards distinguish recorded asset units from supplied monetary valuations. A swap's analytical proceeds and incoming basis do not imply a cash payment. In-kind rewards add income and basis when their value is supplied, without an external contribution. Own-custody transfers preserve original lots; staking and unstaking do not recognize the same reward twice.

Asset fees remove units once and expense FIFO carrying cost under the import's versioned portfolio policy. That expense is not an inferred market sale. Internal transfers and swaps cancel before valuing whole-portfolio flows. A selected subset may still need a transfer-date price or swap valuation. Thus portfolio gain can be supported while a particular lot cost, gain component or subset return remains unknown. See transaction import for evidence and review.
