docs.title: Add or edit a holding
docs.text:
In Positions, choose Add position. Search for an investment and use Select investment, or Choose listing when several exchanges are grouped under a verified ISIN. Verify the exchange and trading currency. Enter manually opens identity fields without requiring search. Change investment reopens search while retaining your quantity, cost and allocation draft. Select an existing instrument when recording it in another account so its identity is reused. The name and price ticker appear together in one row. You can edit the name; a searched ticker is read-only. Use Change investment for another listing. Saved holdings use Connect live prices to review listing changes. Explicit manual entry permits typing a ticker. Optional ISIN metadata is retained under More details; provider omissions do not prevent ticker-based pricing. Names alone do not identify the same security.

Select a row for details; use its pencil to edit. A rename applies to all account rows for that instrument. Quantities can be fractional and nonnegative. Keep account/portfolio distinctions when the same instrument is held more than once. Enter quantity explicitly; zero keeps a planned position. Decimal points or commas are accepted without thousands separators. Average and total buy-in are visible together, followed by category and its target side by side. Account/broker, manual pricing and other optional fields are under More details. Physical assets using manual valuation keep their current price visible.

Buy-in and targets are optional. A successful save writes to the active private workspace. A stale form is rejected; reload it before saving again.

For assets without provider prices, supply a manual unit price with its currency, date and quantity unit. A manual price overrides provider quotes; clearing it restores provider pricing. Instrument type and underlying exposure are distinct: an ETF may hold equity, non-equity or an unknown mixture.

docs.title: Record the cost of the remaining holding
docs.text:
Enter Average buy-in per unit or Total buy-in, with the acquisition currency. The other cost updates automatically. The last cost field you edited stays fixed when quantity changes; the caption identifies it. Clear buy-in removes both amounts. Unchanged saved amounts retain their precision.

Total buy-in is the cost of the quantity still held, including purchase fees; it is not lifetime deposits. The app divides total cost by quantity to obtain average cost. Positive total cost needs a positive quantity. Blank cost remains unknown and does not prevent allocation analysis.

New buy-ins default to the portfolio reporting currency; existing records keep their original currency. Quote currency and buy-in currency can differ. For a foreign-currency buy-in, supply a purchase date, exchange rate or converted total cost. Rates are labelled as reporting-currency units per original currency unit. Missing information can be saved, with gains excluded and a warning. Latest-FX approximations require explicit confirmation and remain labelled.

Use a single date only when it applies to the whole cost. For purchases on different dates, enter separate purchase rows or supply their combined converted cost. After sales, transfers or splits, reconcile the remaining quantity and cost with your records. This summary editor does not infer sales or realized gains. Use transaction history to record sales and calculate FIFO carrying costs and realized gains; it is not a tax-lot reporting service.

docs.title: Replace balances
docs.text: Use Positions → Update balances for several current summaries at once. Review quantities and optional buy-ins, select average or total cost entry, then confirm and save the snapshot. Repeating a balance snapshot replaces quantities; it does not add purchases. Targets and classifications stay saved. Quantity confirmation dates are distinct from purchase dates and market-price timestamps. Changed quantities or buy-ins replace active cost components and invalidate incompatible conversions; they do not infer sales or splits. Metadata-only edits preserve conversions.

docs.title: Calculate a new holding from purchases
docs.text:
In Add position → More details, enable Calculate from purchases. Enter one row per purchase with quantity, unit price, optional date and optional fees. An optional FX rate records reporting-currency units per buy-in currency unit; otherwise dated purchases use historical conversion when available. Missing conversions exclude gains, while available current values remain included. Use one buy-in currency throughout. The quantity and cost fields above become read-only and show the calculated result, including fees. Missing purchase prices keep the resulting cost unknown. Invalid rows must be corrected before saving.

Disabling purchase entry restores the manual quantity and cost draft; purchase rows remain available for this session. Closing and resuming the dialog retains the draft. Cancel discards it. Save position saves the holding, metadata and purchase records together once. These must be purchases making up the current holding without intervening sales or splits; sales accounting is not supported. For additional purchases into an existing position, use Bulk add purchases. An activated transaction history routes purchases to its history editor instead.

docs.title: Add a purchase batch
docs.text:
Open Bulk add purchases for one instrument/account/portfolio. Enter rows, paste spreadsheet cells or upload a UTF-8 CSV/TSV. These figures are invented:

date,shares,price,fees
2026-01-01,2,100,1
2026-02-01,3,120,2

This batch adds five shares and costs 563 currency units, averaging 112.60 per share. Dates are optional ISO dates; quantities must be positive. Blank fees are zero; blank prices are unknown. Use one selected currency per batch; later batches may use different currencies. The optional fx_rate column supplies a conversion rate to the current reporting currency for each row. Mixed-currency totals are displayed in reporting currency; original amounts remain saved. Decimal points or commas are supported without thousands separators; quote decimal commas in comma-delimited CSV or use tabs/semicolons.

Add new purchases increases shares. Calculate buy-in for shares already held leaves quantity unchanged and requires purchases accounting for all current shares with no intervening sales or splits. Review the before/after preview, then save once. Repeated batches require acknowledgment; identical rows within one batch all count. Unknown opening cost or a missing purchase price keeps the resulting cost unknown.

After a balance replacement, additional purchase dates must be after the balance confirmation date. Retained batches are context, not a complete transaction ledger; do not sum old and recalculated batches to reconstruct the holding.

docs.title: Physical gold
docs.text: In Add position → Physical asset → Gold spot price, enter fine-gold weight in troy ounces, grams or kilograms. One troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams. The app retrieves gold spot in USD per troy ounce, converts the quantity and values it in the selected portfolio currency. Prices represent fine-gold spot value, without coin/bar premiums or dealing costs. Gold spot history is not yet supported. Manual pricing remains available; existing manual holdings only switch when you explicitly choose live spot pricing.

docs.title: Calendar layout
docs.text: Date pickers show Monday through Sunday by default. Choose Portfolio settings → Week starts on to switch between Monday and Sunday. This preference is saved with the portfolio and applies to its date pickers without changing recorded dates.

docs.title: Optional transaction history
docs.text:
To find gaps across current positions, open Positions → History. It shows positions needing attention by default; clear that filter to see every position. The list separates absent or unapplied transactions, missing transaction details, and missing market inputs. Select a row to open its transaction review, holdings history or account journal. Checks use saved evidence and the recorded interval; matching balances alone cannot prove that no transactions are missing. Ordinary interior price gaps do not themselves make a position incomplete.

Total quantity and average buy-in remain sufficient for current portfolio analysis. Open a position's Transactions view to start an empty list with Add buy or Add sell. Other transaction supports distributions, splits, transfers and fees. Save transaction retains incomplete work without changing the current holding. You can enter purchases and sales before deciding how much history you can reconstruct.

Import PDFs accepts a batch of Consorsbank stock/ETF buy and sale statements for the selected position and account (up to 100 PDFs / 100 MB per batch, 20 MB per file). Files are read locally; original PDFs are not stored in history or sent to a service. Ready statements are hidden by default; Show ready statements reveals them. Problems and statements needing review come first, with newest dates first within each group. Ready, review and excluded counts always describe the whole batch; hiding a ready statement does not exclude it. Select a table row to inspect its amounts or change Include this transaction. Identical imports and invalid statements cannot be included. Similar trades start excluded; Import as a separate trade confirms only that statement, not the rest of the batch. Statement details include the identifier, taxes and settlement amount. If the position has no stored ISIN/WKN, check the document identifier yourself before saving; a filename or instrument name alone does not establish a match. When no identifier can be compared, I checked the instrument identifiers is required before saving. A known ISIN or WKN mismatch cannot be overridden. Legacy WKN-only statements are supported when the quoted price has an explicit currency; a currency-free quote still requires manual entry. For parsing failures, Statement details → Download masked layout report creates a local text report containing fixed financial labels, token types and reconciliation checks. It identifies which rows were parsed and which amounts match a settlement discrepancy without exporting those amounts; a match is a diagnostic clue, not an automatically applied correction. The report lists blocking parser issues and distinguishes exact settlement or quoted-price matches from nonzero differences within the rounding tolerance. Recognized order limits and tax calculation or allowance balances are labelled as informational and retain page/row references. They do not change execution prices or become transaction charges. Unexpected amounts on those rows still require review. It omits filenames, metadata and original names, identifiers, dates and amounts. Statement details also lists the page and visual row for each extracted field, including each fee/tax and conflicting candidates. Rows are counted from the top of each page. Compact source locations and the quoted price remain in saved transaction notes; raw extracted rows and original PDFs are not retained. Review the report before sharing it for troubleshooting; it does not upload anything or establish that the extracted financial values are correct. The Document column beside File in Statement details maps report numbers to local filenames for the current upload batch. Filenames stay out of the masked report. Reordering or changing the upload batch can change document numbers. Complete hexadecimal document-reference codes, including margin text, appear as <document-reference> in the report. They are not transaction amounts; other amounts on the same row still require classification.

Identical files already imported anywhere in this portfolio are blocked. Similar trades are excluded by default and need explicit confirmation if they are distinct. Known instrument mismatches, ambiguous amounts, inconsistent totals, scanned or unsupported statements require manual entry. Corrections/reissues and currency conversion statements need separate review; this is not universal broker support. Unexplained transaction amounts, unsupported signs/refunds, repeated financial totals, extra amounts within a field, and a debit/credit direction contradicting the trade block saving. Confirming fee completeness cannot override these errors. Amounts without a currency also block when embedded in a financial field or accompanied by a charge label, including whole-number charges. Settlement rows recognize labelled German IBANs (compact or grouped) and legacy Konto-Nr. account numbers; other account layouts require manual entry. Separate tax-calculation bases are not tax charges; explicitly listed joint-account tax charges are each retained, even when their amounts agree. After settlement, unfamiliar single amounts inside a recognized tax-detail section and separately labelled ST quantities are supplementary context. Check statement shows their actual extracted text and page/row locations locally, beside the trade value, fees, taxes and settlement. They do not supply execution quantities, fees or taxes. This allows new explanatory labels without adding a parser rule for each one. Sections end at page boundaries, new trade headings or footer headings; arbitrary amounts elsewhere remain blocking. Explicit charges, corrections, malformed known fields and extra amounts remain subject to validation even inside supplementary sections.

Reconciliation checks gross plus charges against a purchase debit, or gross minus charges against sale proceeds. It never fills a difference with an invented fee or tax. Matching totals cannot establish what an unfamiliar row means. Supplementary rows therefore prevent automatic charge confirmation: review the displayed rows and confirm that statement, or explicitly keep its charges unchecked.

Listed fees/taxes are retained separately. A complete, unambiguous buy or sale with explicit debit/credit direction and an exactly reconciled settlement establishes the statement charges automatically. This includes fee-free savings plans, purchases with commissions, and sales with listed tax deductions. It requires fully parsed financial rows and no unresolved supplementary amounts; matching totals alone are insufficient. A buy is not assumed tax-free merely because it is a purchase. Separately billed costs need their own expense records.

When a statement needs review, inspect the displayed additional rows. Tax bases, allowances and explanatory quantities are not additional payments. If all actual charges are included, choose Confirm statement charges. To retain uncertain history, choose Keep charges unchecked, or exclude the transaction. Decisions apply only to that statement; the save summary identifies any unchecked charges. Not listed means no amount was extracted, not that another tax is expected. An absent charge on an automatically reconciled or explicitly confirmed statement is shown as zero. No generic batch confirmation certifies other statements. Unsupported signs, refunds, fields and settlement discrepancies remain blocking where required by parser validation; confirmation never bypasses them.

The original PDFs and additional-row text remain transient local review inputs. Saved history retains parsed transaction amounts and source locations, not raw rows or PDFs. Statement details contains document identifiers and the optional masked troubleshooting report. Statement amounts require recognized ISO currency codes; custody references and bank/page identifiers are not amounts. Unsupported historical currency codes require manual entry.

Save transactions and review retains the batch atomically and opens the usual reconciliation below. It does not add shares to the current holding or activate history. Trade times order same-day imported records where available; otherwise upload order is retained and must be checked in the history review. Cancel/back before saving changes no portfolio data. Concurrent portfolio edits reject a stale save and preserve the uploaded draft for review.

Edit transaction opens a form directly from this list. Choose the transaction, change its date, quantity, amount or fees, then Save changes. The original record is retained, and a correction affects the holding only after review and application. The list shows the latest version, with pending edits labelled. Money is displayed to two decimal places; the editor and calculations retain the full saved precision. Complex starting lots remain available in the advanced editor.

When ready, choose Review against portfolio. By default, the selected records start with your first purchase and zero shares beforehand. This assumption is shown in the review; use Review options → Add starting balance if you already owned shares before the earliest recorded transaction. Applying history records the zero boundary at the end of the day before the earliest transaction or fee; merely opening the review saves nothing and does not invent a purchase. The internal zero boundary is not a transaction and is omitted from the transaction list and the Included transactions picker. Review options also lets you change which records are included and optionally link a cash account.

Alternatively, Add starting balance records a dated, known quantity and optional total acquisition cost when earlier transactions are unavailable. It is optional, and saving it also leaves the current holding unchanged. A starting balance is an end-of-day boundary; its acquisition cost is separate from the market value used to start performance measurement. Earlier transactions are not inferred.

The review compares shares, remaining acquisition cost and average buy-in with the current portfolio, and checks linked cash where applicable. Apply history accepts the displayed holding and linked cash changes as the authoritative ledger. No separate acceptance checkbox is needed. Backfilled shares are not added to the current holding a second time. Resolve discrepancies by correcting records or explicitly accepting the reconstructed balance; Keep portfolio unchanged leaves saved transactions available for later review. Replace balance starts a new interval for an already active history. Advanced record, lot and fee editing is available under Edit transactions, starting lots and fees; earlier records and corrections remain in its Retained evidence view.

Double-click a transaction to edit it directly, or use its Edit button. The list opens newest first; click Date to reverse the order.

To remove transactions, select rows in the Transactions table and choose Remove selected. The header checkbox selects all rows; starting balances are kept and edited separately. Confirm the selected entries before removal. Applied transactions also show the resulting holding and linked cash changes; invalid remaining histories cannot be applied. Unapplied entries leave portfolio balances unchanged. Original evidence is retained internally, and a removed PDF can be imported again. Re-uploading a PDF that is still present does not overwrite it. Removing the last transaction restores the empty entry view without an empty table.

The quantity comparison uses the smaller of one billionth of a unit and one billionth of the recorded quantity. Comparable costs use a one-cent tolerance. These tolerances label differences; they never manufacture an adjustment. Unknown or incompatible converted costs are shown as unknown, not as agreement. Opening History automatically loads available dated prices and FX in the background, from the beginning of recorded history through today. A reconstructed purchase/sale history opens this view even before its first prices have loaded; snapshot-only positions keep the existing clean default. Saved observations are reused on later visits. Failed refreshes retain them and offer Retry prices. FX currencies come from saved transactions and observed price currency. Manual observations are preserved, and downloads never create transactions. Missing prices, FX or transaction records still need to be supplied. Personal value uses the shares held on each date and prices in that date's traded share units; split-normalized asset-chart prices cannot be reused blindly. Offline synthetic demos do not start automatic market requests.

In Transactions → Review against portfolio, compare the reconstructed units and costs, then choose Apply history. For multiple holdings, use Accept this holding for each reviewed balance and Apply reviewed holdings to save the batch. Applying makes that history authoritative for the resulting position: a one-share history replaces a two-share balance with one share. Reapplying does not add those shares again.

There is no separate history confirmation. New valuation dates and changes in chart period do not require reapproval. Gains and returns use the applied records; missing prices, FX, amounts or required starting balances still limit the affected metrics. A starting snapshot does not invent earlier transactions. Incomplete gain history identifies actual missing evidence or limited scope, with details in its tooltip. Supplied estimates remain labelled.

Transaction entry offers Unit price, Trade value (excluding fees) and Total paid (including fees) for purchases or Total received (after fees) for sales. Always enter Fees separately: cash totals already include those fees, so they are not added or deducted again. Enter 0 for no fees; blank means unknown. There is no separate fee-confirmation checkbox for new transactions.

When an earlier saved transaction has unconfirmed fees, Complete transaction fees in the review lets you supply or confirm them. It saves a correction and retains the original record without changing the holding until you apply history. Cost and average buy-in remain unknown when required costs or FX are missing; the review explains the missing input. Complete exchange rates accepts a manual rate for each missing date without using current FX. Applying history is disabled while the reconstructed cost or affected cash balance is unknown.

Fees can have their own currency and date; Starting lots, fees and taxes supports multiple fees and recorded taxes. The old purchase-batch editor retains its established blank-fee-means-zero convention. Purchase fees enter acquisition cost once; sale fees reduce proceeds. Explicit taxes are separate expenses, not additions to the remaining FIFO acquisition cost.

Sales use FIFO for analytical remaining costs. Enter actual opening lots where known. A snapshot's aggregate cost is not an invented set of purchase lots: a partial disposal from unknown opening lots leaves remaining cost unknown. Supply lot evidence or a cost row to reconcile the remaining total; that total does not establish individual lots for another partial disposal. A split row's quantity is the ratio of new units to old units. Internal transfers preserve known lot provenance and require a destination history for the same instrument. transfer_in and transfer_out record movements across the portfolio boundary; supply their dated market value separately from any known acquisition costs.

A linked cash account is maintained once by the account journal. Trade and charge postings are derived from the selected securities records. Payments on or before an account's cash opening are already included in that opening. Explicit deferred claims remain separate until received or paid. Later settlement creates a claim until Accounts & futures → Cash & financing → Receive pending cash records receipt/payment. Do not also enter the same trade payment as a manual cash adjustment. Without linked cash, position-level purchases and sale proceeds cross the selected position's investment boundary.

Activated holdings obtain current quantities and costs from history. Use Replace balance for a summary replacement, and Rebalance for category/target edits. Update balances continues to edit snapshot-only positions. Closed histories remain saved. External edits to an activated holding's original CSV balance are rejected rather than silently overriding its history.

Legacy purchase batches remain unchanged. Copy batch to evidence makes a reviewable candidate with a stable reference to its original row. Cost recalculations may overlap purchases; inspect the selected rows and acknowledge any genuinely distinct matching transactions before activation.

docs.text: Frozen candidate documentation · app 0.2.0 · source b810ada068f870d1319373d5258f456777f389f6

docs.title: Rebalance
docs.text: Configure targets, then open Rebalance → Plan. The default Portfolio contribution scope offers Contribution and Options, then Calculate plan. To use Rebalancing mode, select Within a category and choose a Planning category. Legacy portfolios without categories show the mode selector directly. Source instrument/account rows are the tradable units; Overview/Exposure filters and ETF display groups do not alter this scope.

docs.title: Choose scope and mode
docs.text:
Within-category planning uses that category's post-contribution value. Portfolio contributions first allocate budgets across categories and then within them. Required sibling targets must be complete and total 100%; unrelated category position targets are unnecessary for a within-category plan. Relevant valuations must be complete. Protected categories and their descendants cannot be sold.

The following modes apply within a category (or to a legacy whole portfolio):

Mode Meaning Fewest trades (buys and sells) Reach target ranges without new money, minimizing changed rows before turnover. Minimum new money (no sells) Find the smallest fully invested contribution reaching all ranges, then minimize trades. Allocate new money Allocate a specified budget subject to chosen constraints and distribution.

For selected buys, Rebalance selected positions accounts for current holdings and minimizes squared gaps to exact targets. Spread by target weights divides new money proportionally without accounting for existing holdings. Optimize rebalancing minimizes deviation outside ranges and may concentrate the budget in one position. These distributions serve different purposes.

docs.title: Purchase rules and tolerances
docs.text:
Portfolio contribution defaults to 500 in the reporting currency, all positions eligible, Allow skipping positions, and a minimum purchase of 25. Category and position tolerances each start at ±0.5 percentage points. Within-category Allocate new money uses New money, and exposes the distribution controls below when Limit buys to selected positions is enabled. Its selected-position distribution defaults to Buy every selected position.

Buy every selected position requires its minimum purchase for each row; insufficient budgets produce a shortfall. Allow skipping positions permits a subset, still respecting minimum buys. Prefer fewer trades can accept a specified extra RMS target gap compared with the best plan under the trade limit. That allowance is separate from target tolerance.

Absolute tolerance is in percentage points; relative tolerance is a percentage of the target. An invented 10% target with ±0.5 pp or ±5% relative tolerance has an allowed range of 9.5–10.5%. A zero target has zero relative tolerance.

Only buy existing positions forbids buys into zero-quantity rows while keeping their targets. Exclude empty positions and redistribute targets instead redistributes their targets within each category for the calculation. It does not change saved targets. An empty category retains planned capacity.

Temporary maximum allocations state their denominator: selected category or whole portfolio, using final value including unallocated contribution. Blank means no cap. Caps do not rewrite targets or force sales in a buy-only plan. Conflicts with minimum buys or required purchases produce an explanation.

docs.title: Interpret the result
docs.text:
Suggested trades contains buys/sells; Portfolio impact compares sibling category weights. Plan details includes hold rows, budgets and trade-count comparisons. Unallocated money remains in the final denominator. Reserved category budgets can remain partly uninvested because of purchase constraints. The preview does not create a saved cash holding.

Synthetic offline example with the default contribution options: the 500 EUR budget produces three suggested purchases. Compare Invested contribution with Unallocated cash, then inspect Portfolio impact and Plan details. Calculation places no orders and saves no quantity changes. Open the image for detail.

Deviation outside allowed ranges can be zero even when positions are not exactly on target. RMS gap measures distance from exact targets. Review both with the unallocated amount and scope. Infeasible constraints or an unproven optimizer result produce no plan.

Plans are read-only. They assume fractional quantities and exclude fees, taxes, spreads and lot-size restrictions. No orders are placed and holdings are not updated. After executing your own trades, update quantities/costs separately.

docs.title: Data formats
docs.text: Use the task guides for normal app operation. This page describes private file formats and calculation contracts for advanced editing and development. Back up the workspace and stop the app before editing files externally. All numeric examples here are invented; instrument identities are public metadata.

docs.title: Edit your data
docs.text:
holdings.csv has one row per position. Required columns are id, name, and shares; optional columns are ticker, isin, acquisition_price, portfolio, account, acquisition_currency, and target_allocation. The app-managed purchase_history column stores bulk-entry records and is excluded from filters and allocations. Other additional text columns become metadata filters and allocation dimensions. Calculation output names are reserved: these include position_id, asset_id, asset_name, value, source_*, direct_or_indirect, analysis_asset_*, reporting_currency and calculated price, FX, value, cost, gain and performance fields. A conflicting column produces an error identifying the name to change; the application never renames or rewrites it automatically. Shares must be finite and nonnegative; zero-share positions are allowed. Acquisition price is optional and is displayed as entered.

id,name,ticker,isin,shares,acquisition_price,portfolio,account
example,Example Company,DEMO,,1,10.00,Demo portfolio,Demo account

The stable id identifies an instrument. You may repeat it across account or portfolio rows; its name, ticker, and ISIN must be consistent. Holdings remain separate positions in the table and merge by asset ID for holding allocation. Different exchange listings need distinct IDs. Blank tickers are allowed; without a manual price or supported gold-spot source, a nonzero holding stays unvalued. Ordinary listing prices are looked up using tickers, not ISINs. Tickers and ISINs are trimmed and normalized to uppercase on loading, including tickers displayed in holding selectors and allocation charts. Stable IDs remain unchanged so classification links are preserved.

docs.title: Strategic and legacy targets
docs.text:
Current category-based portfolios use version 2 allocation.yaml for the category tree, bucket_id for each position's leaf category, and within_bucket_target for its fraction of that category. Category targets are relative to their parent; global targets multiply the fractions along that path. Configure these through Rebalance → Targets.

The following whole-portfolio target_allocation rules describe legacy portfolios without strategic allocation. They are not a substitute for within-category targets in current portfolios.

To display legacy targets, add an optional target_allocation column. Enter a fraction such as 0.15 or a percentage such as 15%; leave unavailable values blank. Targets apply to each position as a share of the whole portfolio. The holdings table shows the column only when at least one selected position has a target, keeps missing targets blank, and does not renormalize targets when filtering. Targets are not metadata filters or inferred from current weights. Split a holding's target across its account rows if you maintain multiple positions.

Allocation tables derive label and hierarchy targets by summing the underlying position targets, using the same membership splits as current allocations. Target (% of portfolio) and Current (% of portfolio) share the whole-portfolio basis. Current − target (pp) is positive above target and negative below. Filtering narrows the contributing positions without rescaling their targets. Parent targets include their descendants; do not sum parent and child rows together.

ETF look-through distributes an ETF target using the snapshot's constituent weights, including residual Other. Targets from direct positions and ETF constituents combine by asset identity. The optional SMH display group sums its fund and stock targets. If any contributing position lacks a target, the target and gap stay blank and a Known target subtotal (%) shows the available portion. An explicit zero target is complete. Missing portfolio prices leave the whole- portfolio current comparison and gap blank while preserving known targets.

You can save a position with zero shares and a nonzero target to plan a new investment. Its current value is zero without requiring a quote, and its target contributes to its labels immediately. Add classification labels for new assets in the private YAML file; otherwise they appear under Unclassified.

Zero-unit positions are hidden by default. The header’s Portfolio settings → Show sold positions reveals them in Overview’s positions list, Positions and Exposure, including planned positions with no units. History, realized gains and targets are retained. The separate Rebalance option Exclude empty positions and redistribute targets removes zero-share rows from the planning calculation. Their combined target is divided equally among remaining unique asset IDs within each category (or the whole legacy portfolio), then equally among each asset’s held account rows. This is an equal percentage-point increment, not a proportional scaling. For example, removing an invented 20% planned target adds 10 pp to each of two remaining assets. Saved positions and targets remain unchanged and editable in Positions. Visibility never changes targets. Redistribution requires complete targets if any targets have been entered; it never treats an unknown target as zero. With no targets, the option simply hides empty positions.

docs.title: Planning contracts
docs.text:
The default strategic Rebalance → Plan → Portfolio contribution allocates a contribution across categories and then positions. It defaults to allowing skipped positions, with a minimum purchase of 25 in the reporting currency. Choose Within a category to access the following three modes. Legacy portfolios show these modes directly for the whole portfolio:

  • Fewest trades (buys and sells) reaches every target range with no new money, minimizing changed position/account rows first and total turnover second.
  • Minimum new money (no sells) finds the smallest fully invested contribution that reaches every range, then minimizes trades at that contribution.
  • Allocate new money fully invests a given amount using at most the chosen number of trades. It minimizes the sum of distances outside target ranges, then trade count, then distance from exact targets. A comparison table and plan selector show whether additional trades offer enough improvement.

In Allocate new money, enable Limit buys to selected positions and choose the instrument/account rows in Positions eligible for buying. Then choose Distribution:

  • Rebalance selected positions (default for a selected subset): account for current holdings and final portfolio value, prioritizing larger shortfalls. Minimize the sum of squared percentage-point gaps to exact targets under your purchase constraints. Tolerance ranges affect the reported status, not this split. Configure Selection intent and Minimum purchase (reporting currency):
  • Buy every selected position (default): buy at least the minimum amount for every selected row, including overweight and zero-target rows. The initial minimum is 25 in the portfolio currency and can be changed. Insufficient budgets show the required contribution and shortfall; positions are never silently skipped.
  • Allow skipping positions: choose the best allocation, with every suggested buy meeting the minimum. Prefer fewer trades is off by default. Enable it to set Maximum trades and compare allocation quality across trade counts. Allowed extra target error (pp) defaults to 0.1 pp: choose the fewest trades whose root mean squared (RMS) target gap is within that amount of the best plan under the cap. Zero allows no additional error. The suggested plan is selected initially; any comparison plan can be inspected.
  • Limit allocations for this rebalance (within Rebalance selected positions): enter an optional Maximum allocation (%) for each selected instrument/account row. Blank means no cap; zero prevents further buys. The cap uses the selected denominator (portfolio or category), including the contribution and any unallocated cash. Saved targets keep guiding the allocation and are never overwritten by temporary caps. A position already above its cap receives no buys; this buy-only calculation does not force a sale. A cap that conflicts with Buy every selected position or Minimum purchase produces an explanation. Caps reset when the selection changes and are not saved to portfolio files. The calculator invests as much as the caps, minimum buys and trade limit allow, then minimizes squared target gaps. Remaining money appears as Unallocated cash, included in the percentage denominator; displayed position percentages may total less than 100%. Fewer-trade suggestions preserve the maximum amount that can be invested; comparison rows also show each plan's unallocated cash.
  • Spread by target weights: divide the contribution in proportion to the selected eligible targets. For example, invented targets of 20% and 10% receive two thirds and one third of the new money. Zero targets receive nothing.
  • Optimize rebalancing: choose buys that improve the whole portfolio's allocation, with a trade limit and trade-count comparison. This can put the entire contribution into one position.

RMS target gap is the square root of the mean squared percentage-point gap across the position rows in the selected planning scope. It measures the squared-deviation objective on a readable scale; it is separate from deviation outside tolerance ranges. Without caps, for a fixed number of buys with a uniform minimum, buying the largest target shortfalls is optimal. With caps, candidate choices also account for the remaining capacity of each position. The calculator compares feasible trade counts, including when all positions are in range.

Only Spread by target weights ignores existing holdings when splitting the contribution. Minimum-purchase and selection-intent controls apply to Rebalance selected positions. Both distributions allocate whole cents of reporting currency so buys plus any unallocated cash sum to the budget. Target-weight splitting rejects an amount too small to fund every positive-weight recipient with at least one cent. Only buy existing positions excludes selected rows with zero shares. If this conflicts with Buy every selected position, deselect those rows, allow skipping, or turn off Only buy existing positions; the calculator explains the conflict. Unselected positions receive no trades. Final weights and deviation still use targets in the planning scope, so spreading can leave positions outside their ranges. Changing the selection or distribution hides stale plans. Changing position identities clears the selection for you to choose again. These controls apply only to Allocate new money and never change saved holdings or targets.

Choose an absolute tolerance (default ±0.5 percentage points) or a percentage relative to each target. For a 10% target, ±0.5 pp and ±5% relative both allow 9.5–10.5%. Relative tolerance leaves a zero target at zero; absolute tolerance can allow a small holding. Bounds are clipped to 0–100%.

Within-category rebalancing requires position targets totaling 100% of that category; legacy planning requires whole-portfolio targets totaling 100%. Both require complete valuations in their scope and use final weights including the contribution. Portfolio contributions also require complete category targets. Overview filters, label selections and ETF display groups do not alter the tradable positions. Only buy existing positions forbids buying zero-share account rows while retaining their targets; Exclude empty positions and redistribute targets instead removes and redistributes them before calculation. Infeasible restrictions produce an explanation.

Amounts assume fractional shares and exclude fees, taxes, spreads and lot-size constraints. New money is fully invested except when temporary allocation caps and purchase restrictions leave an unallocated remainder. This is a calculation result, not a saved cash account. Reporting-currency amounts are rounded only for display. Plans never place orders or write holdings. SciPy’s HiGHS linear/mixed-integer optimizer must report a proven optimum; a solver limit or failed constraint check produces no trade plan. Each solve has a ten-second limit; interactive calculations support up to 100 position rows. With zero invested capital, choose a budget in Allocate new money instead of asking for a minimum contribution.

docs.title: Classification format
docs.text:
classifications.yaml maps asset IDs to any number of named taxonomies:

nvda:
  classifications:
    ai:
      - [AI, Compute, GPUs]
    sector:
      - [Technology, Semiconductors]
    geography:
      - [North America, United States]

Taxonomy names and tree depths are unrestricted by application logic. Add asset class, tags, sleeves, or other custom classifications using the same format. Keep the file present; {} is valid when you have no classifications yet. Missing membership in a selected taxonomy appears as Unclassified.

An asset with several distinct paths splits its value equally across them. Identical repeated paths are deduplicated. Explicit path weights are deferred. Full paths identify categories, so repeated labels under different parents stay separate. When an internal category also has its own allocation, an Assigned here leaf preserves that value in the visualization. At a truncated depth, short paths remain visible instead of disappearing.

Use Positions in the app to create and edit positions, or edit the CSV outside the app and reload the page. Classification trees remain editable in YAML. File data is read on each Streamlit rerun.

docs.title: Portfolio currency storage
docs.text:
portfolio.yaml stores version 1 settings with reporting_currency (EUR, USD or GBP). An absent file means EUR; opening a legacy workspace does not rewrite it. The optional app-managed cost_basis_details holdings column stores versioned active cost components, original currencies and target-specific conversions. It is excluded from classification/filter dimensions and exposure payloads. Legacy purchase batches remain readable. Their dates are used only if the recorded history reconciles with the current summary. External balance edits supersede incompatible purchase evidence instead of inventing disposal accounting.

Calculated reporting amounts use currency-neutral interfaces: current_value_reporting, cost_basis_reporting, unrealized_gain_reporting and reporting_currency. Original native cost and return fields remain separate. Monetary table keys are currency-neutral; the interface identifies their active reporting currency. Include the complete private workspace in backups, including settings and cost records. These files must never be committed to Git.

For architecture, tests and preview commands, see Source development.

docs.title: Release and upgrade notes
docs.text: Frozen candidate documentation · app 0.2.0 · source b810ada068f870d1319373d5258f456777f389f6

docs.title: Version 0.2.0
docs.text: Version 0.2.0 extends current-holdings analysis with optional transaction history, personal performance, monitoring, and manually recorded futures and accounts. Existing holdings remain usable without adding transactions. The application continues to run locally; it does not connect to brokerage accounts, execute orders or calculate taxes.

docs.title: Transaction history and balances
docs.text:
CSV, supported PDF statements and manual transactions use the same retained evidence and review workflow. Save evidence without changing balances, or review the reconstructed holdings and explicitly apply them. Each affected holding must be reviewed before the final combined apply. Applied history becomes authoritative for that holding's quantity and cost; reapplying it does not add the trades to the old balance again. New imports can choose a category independently of instrument type, including holdings already fully sold. Existing categories and targets remain intact.

Exact reimports preserve existing decisions. Similar legitimate trades remain available for review, while changed source records require correction review. Edits and removals retain their original evidence, including changes affecting multiple assets. An opening snapshot establishes a boundary; it does not invent earlier transactions or prove an earlier zero balance. Review the stated starting point before applying an export that begins after you already owned assets.

Closed positions retain their transactions, categories, targets and supported gains. Portfolio settings → Show sold positions reveals them in the relevant lists. Hiding them does not erase history or redistribute targets. A zero-unit holding needs no current price to establish its zero current value.

docs.title: Personal value, gains and returns
docs.text:
Performance uses dated holdings, external cash flows, prices and FX where available. The measures answer different questions:

Measure Meaning Remaining acquisition cost and unrealized gain Cost still attached to the holding, and current value less that supported cost Realized gain, income and total known gain Supported historical components; a known subtotal does not imply complete lifetime results Period gain Ending market value less opening market value and net external contributions Time-weighted return (TWR) Linked investment returns using supported flow boundaries; ordinary calculations use the documented daily convention Annualized money-weighted return (XIRR) A uniquely verified annualized rate using dated external cash flows and endpoint values

Allocation's percentage gain uses full-history TWR, not a silently shortened chart period. Overview remembers the chosen view per portfolio across refreshes and restarts. Current value and supported monetary gains can remain available when a percentage return is unavailable.

Internal movements cancel only within the selected scope. Included-cash purchases, transfers between included accounts and futures settlements do not create an extra external contribution. Fees count once. Futures notional, margin and allocated principal are distinct from account equity.

Missing amounts, FX, prices or unsupported prehistory stay unknown. Explicitly supported empty inception and complete liquidation are valid; a snapshot alone does not establish them. TWR requires its flow-boundary evidence. XIRR is withheld when no unique, numerically reliable result is established, including unsupported complex schedules; it is not guaranteed for every ledger. See the calculation requirements for timing, scope and limits.

Historical prices retain source and as-of dates. Documented exchange closures may use the preceding supported close with provenance; missing scheduled closes are not silently filled. Reviewed alternative listings and proxies remain disclosed and do not change the held listing or reconstruct missing trades. Quote provenance preserves or accepts explicitly supplied source, listing, calendar and timezone details for manual historical corrections. Original observations remain retained, and downloads cannot overwrite the manual value.

docs.title: Futures, accounts and monitoring
docs.text:
Futures and leverage supports actual positions, account cash and financing in EUR, USD and GBP, exact-contract settlement evidence and recorded corrections. Settlements relocate profit or loss into cash; they do not create it twice. Account bindings preserve ownership and prevent double counting cash already included in holdings. Hypothetical studies remain separate from actual transactions, and legacy futures simulations are not automatically adopted. New account setup distinguishes an existing-balance snapshot from a newly funded account with explicit zero inception and a dated external contribution. Internal funding between included accounts uses a transfer instead. Futures transaction CSV import remains unsupported; enter those events manually.

Monitoring stores rules, observations and alert state locally. Historical risk estimates and hypothetical funding studies remain distinct from personal realized performance and do not forecast future returns.

docs.title: Upgrade from 0.1.0
docs.text:
1. Record the active workspace shown in Portfolio settings → App & workspace. A remembered restore selection can differ from the original --data-dir. Create and download a complete workspace backup, retain the old application, and stop it before installing the update.
  2. Follow the platform update instructions. Keep portable application files separate from portfolio data and use the same active workspace. No checkout-local data is moved automatically.
  3. Verify the application reports version 0.2.0. Check holdings, reporting currency, categories, targets, ETF data and any saved history before retiring the old installation. Keep the pre-upgrade backup unchanged.
  4. Add history only when wanted. Opening a legacy workspace does not convert purchase batches or apply an inferred ledger. Review balances before applying transactions; existing cost-entry records are not a complete trading history.

Securities-history saves use account journal version 5; this version reads journal versions 1–5. Other documents have their own schema versions. App-managed saves retain document backups, and interrupted combined holdings/history publication has recovery safeguards. These safeguards do not replace a complete backup or make concurrent external editing safe. Close external editors while the app saves or captures a backup.

For rollback, stop the new app, restore the complete pre-upgrade backup into a new workspace, and open that copy with the matching older application. A newer journal may be unreadable by an older app. Do not overwrite your current workspace, copy only an older journal over newer holdings, or assume uninstalling reverses data changes. Changes made after the backup remain in the newer workspace and will not appear in the restored copy. See history compatibility and the recovery options for remembered workspace selection.

Backups include history, observations, source evidence and closed positions along with holdings and settings. For history-managed rows, holdings.csv retains the source snapshot; it is not a standalone export of the latest projected balances. Keep the entire workspace and its unencrypted backups private.

docs.title: Installer limitations
docs.text: Acceptance applies to each published artifact, not to these notes alone. Ubuntu's native package retains its experimental package/menu identity. The Apple Silicon macOS installer remains experimental, with ad-hoc signing, no Developer ID signature or notarization, and unverified personal-Mac download/approval behavior. See installation and the published artifact's acceptance information. Bundled help identifies the exact app source and is available offline; it is not replaced by a newer development guide.

docs.title: Storage and recovery
docs.text: Frozen candidate documentation · app 0.2.0 · source b810ada068f870d1319373d5258f456777f389f6

docs.title: Locate the workspace
docs.text:
The persistent default is independent of the launch directory:

Platform Default Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/portfolio-breakdown/portfolio, normally ~/.local/share/portfolio-breakdown/portfolio Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\portfolio-breakdown\portfolio macOS ~/Library/Application Support/portfolio-breakdown/portfolio

Open Portfolio settings → App & workspace to see the active folder and use Open data folder to open it in your file manager. A confirmed restore can remember a different active folder for the same shortcut (see below). For a custom launch directory, see advanced launch options.

The workspace contains holdings.csv (including saved purchase/cost records), optional portfolio.yaml currency settings, display-preferences.json calendar preferences, classifications.yaml, strategic allocation.yaml, ETF snapshots under etfs/, private overrides, .cache and per-document .backups. Keep the whole directory private. App-managed saves validate data, check file revisions and back up previous files before atomic replacement. Those backups do not protect against loss of the entire drive.

docs.title: History, futures and account records
docs.text:
Version 0.2.0 also keeps these private documents in the same workspace:

Document Contents monitoring.json Saved rules and revisions, recorded metric observations, alert episodes and read/acknowledgment state account-journal.json Optional securities records, reviewed history selections and dated capital allocations; accounts, exact contract definitions, position identities, dated transactions and corrections, cash/holding bindings, collateral reservations and entered margin requirements settlement-archive.json Durable exact-contract daily settlement observations, retained source revisions and accepted prices settlement-collection.json Last automatic collection attempts and dated source availability history-observations.json Dated prices, FX, manual total/boundary valuations, correction history and scope coverage reviews account-observations.json Dated valuation marks and manual FX observations; these do not post cash generalized-study-settings.json Named hypothetical scenarios, cash reserves, policies and input assumptions leverage-settings.json Existing leverage settings, legacy liabilities and documented fund exposure factors

Daily settlements are archived separately from the journal and included in workspace backups. Clearing .cache does not remove this archive; closing or rolling a position retains its history. Archive writes retain observation versions in the document rather than creating a full per-download backup copy. Other public history downloads may remain in caches. Eligible daily futures settlements are applied automatically from the archive using their recorded quantities and clearing basis; duplicate dates and manual corrections are preserved. Other market observations do not create transactions. Missing or failed downloads do not justify reconstructing account balances from estimated prices. Keep the whole workspace, including caches and study inputs, private.

When existing cash is adopted by an account, its original holding identity is retained and linked to one native account balance. Account cash replaces that holding's valuation contribution. Subsequent balance changes belong in Futures → Cash & financing, not a second cash holding or an ordinary holdings edit. Linking assets may save persistent position keys without changing their quantities. Security collateral reservations reference owned share/unit quantities; they do not create additional assets.

Transactions preserve original native-currency amounts. Corrections retain the original entries and append replacement/reversal facts. A snapshot can start accounting at a known cash balance and clearing basis without inventing older transactions. Delayed cash remains a recorded claim until an explicit receipt or payment. Changing reporting currency changes valuation, not saved native amounts.

Legacy futures-sandbox.json and its comparison/history/funding settings remain separate simulation documents. They are not automatically converted into actual positions. Adopting a legacy liability records its existing debt and marks the old record as already included, preserving the original settings while preventing duplicate debt. Use the app's reviewed saves to preserve these relationships; copying individual account files between unrelated holdings workspaces can leave invalid references. See Futures and leverage for the workflows.

docs.title: Back up and restore
docs.text:
Open Portfolio settings → Create backup while My portfolio is selected. Wait for verification, then choose Download backup and save the .portfolio-backup.zip file. Browser mode uses the browser download flow; the Windows window uses its native Save dialog. Canceling the download leaves your portfolio unchanged. Unsaved forms are not included.

The versioned archive preserves saved holdings and purchase-cost components/FX, reporting currency, categories and targets, classifications, ETF holdings and substitute baskets, overrides, portfolio caches and hidden document backups. It also preserves the account journal, valuation observations, collateral/account bindings, named study settings and legacy sandbox documents. Restore validates account references against the saved holdings; it does not promote simulated positions into real transactions. Runtime locks and temporary files are excluded. The app briefly coordinates persistent writes while capturing a consistent snapshot; network requests and compression do not hold that barrier. Close external editors first: they cannot participate in the app's locks, and a detected external change aborts the backup. Third-party provider runtime caches are stored separately from portfolio data.

To restore:

  1. Open Portfolio settings → Restore backup and select the archive.
  2. Choose Review backup. The app checks format compatibility, paths, file sizes, checksums and portfolio data before showing the review.
  3. Review the saved currency, position/category/classification/ETF counts and destination. You can edit New workspace folder to another new folder on the computer running the app; its parent must already exist.
  4. Choose Restore and switch. The app creates and verifies that new workspace, then switches in the same window or browser tab. Your old workspace remains intact. Unsaved forms are discarded when switching.

Cancel restore or dismissing the review creates no destination and does not change the active portfolio. Existing destinations are always refused. If files restore successfully but switching fails, the new folder is preserved and Retry switch retries activation. Cancel at that point leaves that verified folder available for later use.

The same shortcut or launch path, including the same --data-dir, remembers the confirmed selection after restart. App & workspace shows the actual active folder. Selection is local application state; it is not embedded in the portable archive. Different original launch paths retain independent selections. Previous workspace leases remain reserved until this app stops, preventing another app from opening a folder still referenced by an old tab or background task.

For recovery only: to open the original launch folder directly, stop that app, then use the installed console companion. See where to run commands and Linux equivalents. Replace the example paths with your folders:

.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\original" --stop
.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\original" --ignore-workspace-selection

This recovery mode ignores the remembered selection without deleting it. It supports backup and editing; restore-and-switch requires a normal launch. A missing/invalid remembered workspace reports an error instead of silently opening a different portfolio. Restore backup also remains available when portfolio currency or holdings files cannot load in an otherwise available folder. The temporary demo and tour cannot create or restore backups.

Backups are private and unencrypted. Store them on another protected device or backup service to protect against drive loss. SHA-256 detects damage; it does not prove who created an archive. Archives are limited to 200 MiB compressed, 1 GiB expanded and 10,000 files. Links, unsafe/non-portable filenames and absolute ETF file references are refused. Unsupported archive versions require a compatible app; they are never silently converted. CSV/Excel Import holdings remains a separate workflow under Positions.

docs.title: Advanced folder-copy commands
docs.text:
Prefer Create backup and Restore backup for everyday use. The installed console companion can also copy complete folders with the app and external editors stopped. Their arguments are directories, not .portfolio-backup.zip archives. Use new destinations:

.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\workspace" --stop
.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\workspace" --backup-to "C:\path\to\new-backup"
.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\new-restored-workspace" --restore-from "C:\path\to\new-backup"
.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\new-restored-workspace"

The backup source follows the remembered selection. Add --ignore-workspace-selection to copy the original folder instead. Folder copies preserve the source and refuse overwrite, symbolic links, external ETF references and changed or invalid data. Open and verify a copied workspace before adopting it.

docs.title: Move an older workspace
docs.text:
No repository-local data is migrated automatically. Stop the app, then copy an old workspace into a new destination using the installed console companion:

.\portfolio-app.exe --data-dir "C:\path\to\new-workspace" --migrate-from "C:\path\to\old-workspace"

The source is retained. Check the copy before removing anything. See update instructions for version rollback and uninstall.

docs.title: Privacy and network access
docs.text:
The application server runs on loopback with Streamlit usage telemetry disabled. Local storage is not encryption. Protect your workspace, backups and exported reports using your operating system's access controls and backup policy.

Ordinary operation requests public quotes/history, FX, instrument search and issuer ETF data. Search text and selected instrument identifiers go to providers; position quantities and purchase costs are not sent as part of those lookups. Import files and review drafts are processed locally. The explicit offline demo avoids market requests; normal demo mode uses the network.

Futures data requests use public product, contract, date, FX and explicitly chosen proxy identifiers. Account cash, contract quantities and manually entered taxes are stored locally; no broker connection is required. Market downloads, account transaction entry and hypothetical studies are separate operations. Futures transaction CSV import is not supported; enter futures transactions manually.

Do not commit personal holdings, accounts, costs, targets, classifications, imports, screenshots, reports, caches, backups or credentials. The entire data/ directory and personal handoff.md are private. Contributor checks are described in Source development. An automated scan cannot recognize all personal details.

docs.title: Transaction-history compatibility
docs.text:
Opening a legacy workspace does not convert its purchase batches or rewrite the journal. Securities-history saves use account journal version 5; dated allocations require at least version 2. Saves retain a private backup. Versions 1–5 remain readable, and existing native futures events preserve their meaning. Older application versions may not read the current journal; use a compatible application or restore the complete pre-upgrade backup into a separate workspace. Do not replace only the journal while retaining newer history.

History-managed CSV rows retain their source snapshot and metadata. Current financial balances are projected from the journal, so the CSV alone is not a current-balance export. Back up the entire workspace. Draft evidence, original records, observations, coverage reviews and closed positions are included. A failed first activation may leave stable position keys, but never a partially applied trade or duplicate cash posting.

See the version 0.2.0 upgrade notes before updating or downgrading an installation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom What to check Browser tab closed but app still runs Relaunch the same shortcut to reopen it, then choose Portfolio settings → App & workspace → Stop application. See launch and stop for recovery commands. Another version or mode opens Stop that workspace's instance before relaunching; verify the executable/checkout and data directory. Explicit port is occupied Use a different port or stop the owning app. Do not stop another workspace blindly. Package fails to start Keep the complete application folder together, including its _internal or _internal-<build> runtime. On Windows, try Portfolio Breakdown (browser) in the Start menu. See startup logs below. Source changes do not appear Restart the owning server after Python module changes; browser refresh alone can leave imported modules stale. Position value is blank Inspect ticker, manual price, quote currency, FX and price status. Buy-in is not a market price. Refresh shows old data Cached fallback preserves the last successful data. Check provider dates separately from retrieval time. Amundi overnight fund reports an unreliable listing For ISIN LU1190417599, use Positions → Connect live prices to review CSH2.PA (Paris) or SMART.MI (Milan). The 0E2B.IL feed is excluded from live prices and history, including old cache entries. Existing quantities and manually supplied prices are retained. Demo cannot initialize Normal demo needs public prices/FX. Retry, or choose ? → Take the tour for an invented offline example. Large Other / whole ETF Inspect coverage, source date and support. A partial or absent breakdown is not a zero holding. Holdings snapshot import is unavailable Only holdings snapshots require an empty portfolio. Choose Transactions to import trades into existing holdings, or Update balances to replace current quantities. Wrong imported decimals or rows Recheck number format, header, worksheet, delimiter and mappings before accepting. Cost/return is blank Check buy-in currency and coverage; unknown is not zero. Risk cannot calculate Check common history, benchmark, exclusions and the 52-week minimum in Risk. Cannot save an old form Another write changed the file. Reload the latest data and reapply the intended edit. Plan is infeasible Review target totals, valuation coverage, minimum buys, protected categories, eligibility and caps. Restore refuses a destination Use a new directory; restore intentionally refuses overwrite.

docs.title: Startup logs
docs.text:
On Windows, the normal Portfolio Breakdown shortcut opens the app window; Portfolio Breakdown (browser) opens it in your default browser. Both use the same local server, so switching presentation may not resolve a server failure.

The window's startup error shows the actual log folder. To open the default location, paste %LOCALAPPDATA%\portfolio-breakdown\window into File Explorer's address bar. Look at the newest window-*.log files: the launcher and server can write separate logs. Browser-launch diagnostics are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\portfolio-breakdown\launcher.log.

If reporting a problem, provide the app version/source commit, operating system, action and a minimal invented reproduction. Review diagnostics before sharing. Share only relevant error lines after removing personal paths and portfolio details; do not attach complete private logs, workspace files or portfolio screenshots. A successful server health response confirms liveness only; check the actual affected view.
